items.title: Physiological and biochemical responses of chestnut cultivars to drought and rewatering
items.authors: Marques T, Ferreira-Pinto A, Pinto T, Gomes-Laranjo J.
items.abstract: Abstract Drought is an increasingly important constraint for chestnut cultivation in Mediterranean regions, where recurrent summer water deficits can restrict plant performance and compromise recovery after stress release. In Castanea sativa Mill., drought resilience depends on the coordinated adjustment of physiological and biochemical traits rather than on the behaviour of a single marker. This study evaluated three Portuguese chestnut cultivars, Judia, Longal, and Martaínha, grafted onto CA-90 rootstock, together with non-grafted CA-90 plants, under controlled drought and rewatering conditions. Plants were assessed at the initial irrigated phase (IP), after 7 days of irrigation withdrawal (NIP), and after 30 days of rewatering (RIP). Net photosynthesis, transpiration, leaf temperature, soluble sugars, starch, soluble proteins, electrolyte leakage, catalase (CAT), ascorbate peroxidase (APX), total phenolic compounds, total flavonoids, and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) were analysed. Drought reduced gas exchange in all plant materials and increased leaf temperature, indicating marked functional impairment under water deficit. Longal and Martaínha maintained comparatively higher physiological performance during drought and showed the strongest recovery after rewatering, whereas CA-90 displayed the lowest gas-exchange rates, greater starch depletion, and higher membrane damage. Soluble sugars, soluble proteins, CAT, and APX increased during drought, while starch declined in all cultivars. In contrast, phenolics, flavonoids, and FRAP decreased under water deficit and recovered partially or substantially after rewatering. items.title: A novel partitivirus induces hypovirulence and increases pyraclostrobin sensitivity in the phytopathogenic fungus Lasiodiplodia ziziphi .
items.authors: Wang Y, Gao X, Xie S, Guo Y, Wu H, Zhou F, Yu H, Zhang M.
items.abstract: Lasiodiplodia ziziphi causes canker disease in jujube and other woody plants. Its control relies mainly on fungicides. Mycoviruses that cause hypovirulence are an emerging option for the biological control of fungal diseases. In this study, we identified a novel double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) mycovirus, Lasiodiplodia ziziphi partitivirus 1 (LzPV1), from L. ziziphi strain CDZM004. The LzPV1 genome consists of two dsRNA segments. dsRNA1 (1,905 bp) encodes an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), and dsRNA2 (1,773 bp) encodes a capsid protein (CP). The genome is packaged into isometric virions about 32 nm in diameter. Phylogenetic analysis of the RdRp and CP placed LzPV1 in the genus Alphapartitivirus of the family Partitiviridae. LzPV1 was transmitted horizontally through hyphal anastomosis and vertically through conidia. LzPV1 infection reduced the virulence of L. ziziphi, changed its hyphal morphology, and increased fungal sensitivity to the fungicide pyraclostrobin. This is the first mycovirus reported in L. ziziphi and the first partitivirus described in the genus Lasiodiplodia. LzPV1 is a promising biocontrol resource for jujube canker disease.

items.title: Multi-omics analyses reveal dynamic interactions between DNA methylation and transcriptional regulation during black raspberry ripening.
items.authors: Hsieh WH, Hung YH, Zhang JH, Cui Q, Chen HY, Lin LP, He MH, Wang YC, Ho YY, Ballington J, Fernandez G, Perkins-Veazie P, H Le B, Li X, Hsieh TF, Lin JY.
items.abstract: Fruit ripening is a complex developmental process involving coordinated changes in gene expression, metabolism, and epigenetic regulation. How DNA methylation dynamics influence gene transcription and metabolite accumulation during black raspberry (Rubus occidentalis) fruit ripening remains poorly understood. Here, we performed developmental-series transcriptome, methylome, and metabolome analysis; the results from this analysis reveal extensive epigenetic reprogramming during black raspberry fruit ripening. Fruit tissues exhibit globally higher DNA methylation than leaves, particularly in CHG and CHH contexts. Local methylation in all cytosine contexts progressively decreases in promoter regions during ripening, whereas CHG and CHH methylation increase in transposon-rich regions. Two primary methylation transitions-promoter hypomethylation and CHH hypermethylation-govern transcriptional shifts in genes involved in ripening processes. Methyl-binding transcription factors with activation potential likely promote CHH hypermethylation-linked transcriptional activation. Multi-omics integration reveals that coordinated anthocyanin accumulation parallels expression of biosynthetic and regulatory genes within coherent networks. Elevated non-CG methylation in heterochromatin coincides with increased transcription of histone variants mediating chromatin compaction, suggesting chromatin remodelers fine-tune accessibility for methyltransferases. Our study highlights both genome-wide and locus-specific epigenetic reprogramming and demonstrates a coordinated interplay between DNA methylation and transcriptional regulation during black raspberry fruit ripening.

items.title: <i>In vitro</i> efficacy of BLAD against <i>Phytophthora cinnamomi</i>: Effects on mycelial growth, sporulation, and zoospore germination of isolates from <i>Quercus suber</i> and <i>Castanea sativa</i>.
items.authors: Trindade M, Machado H, Ferreira RB.
items.abstract: Phytophthora cinnamomi Rands is a devastating soilborne oomycete responsible for root rot in Quercus suber L., Castanea sativa Mill., Quercus ilex L. and many other species worldwide, causing widespread forest decline across Mediterranean ecosystems. The BLAD-containing oligomer (BCO), isolated from Lupinus albus L. cotyledons, is a β-conglutin derived polypeptide oligomer who´s major 20.4 kDa polypeptide BLAD has been reported to exhibit potent and broad-spectrum antifungal and anti-oomycete activity, as well as protective efficacy against P. cinnamomi under greenhouse conditions. However, whether this protection reflects direct pathogen inhibition, host biostimulation or host boosting defense effects remains unresolved, and no in vitro characterization of its anti-P. cinnamomi activity had ever been established. Here, the in vitro activity of a BCO-based commercial formulation (PROBLAD®) was evaluated against five P. cinnamomi isolates (four from Q. suber, one from C. sativa) across multiple endpoints: mycelial radial growth, dry weight, chlamydospore and sporangia production, and zoospore germination. BCO inhibited radial growth in a concentration- and time-dependent manner (EC50: 4.74-6.43 mL/L). At ≥5 mL/L, colonies showed reduced compactness confirmed by dry weight (EC50: 2.63-4.08 mL/L), demonstrating that radial growth underestimates inhibitory activity by not capturing reductions in mycelial density. A transient stimulatory effect (hormesis) was observed at 1-2 mL/L across all isolates. Chlamydospore and sporangia production were fully suppressed at 1-5 mL/L, indicating interference with the induction phase of sporulation. Zoospore germination was inhibited with an EC50 of 5.72 mL/L and completely abolished at 20 mL/L. Microscopic examination revealed progressi…

items.title: The Gibberellin-Responsive Module RsRGL3a-RsGID1b-1-RsATL56 Orchestrates Parthenocarpic Fruit Formation in Seedless Chestnut Rose (Rosa sterilis).
items.authors: Zhou K, Leng Y, Shen L, Min Y, Wen S, Wang Y, Deng L, Peng L, Wang H, Zhong S, Ao Y, Song Z, Yang K, Qiao G, Wen X.
items.abstract: Seedlessness is a fruit trait highly favoured by consumers, with parthenocarpy serving as an important means to achieve seedless fruit. In this work, RsGID1b‐1 responds to GAs and promotes parthenocarpic fruitsetting by activating RsATL56 transcription in seedless chestnut rose ( Rosa sterilis ). RsRGL3a antagonizes RsGID1b‐1 and represses RsATL56 , negatively regulating parthenocarpy.

items.title: Blue Foods of Bihar: Why Its Aquatic Economy Needs an Intelligence Layer
items.authors: Mohan S, Matolia J, Verma S.
items.abstract: Bihar's blue food economy, built on inland fisheries, makhana (fox nut) cultivation, and water chestnut (singhara) farming, is a major contributor to India's aquatic food production and a critical source of rural livelihoods, nutrition, and income. The state ranks fourth among India's inland fish producers, contributes roughly 90% of India's makhana output, and accounts for nearly 60% of the country's water chestnut production. Despite this scale, the sector faces mounting structural risks: climate variability, recurring floods and droughts, rising temperatures, water quality degradation, and disease outbreaks. These risks are compounded by a lack of integrated early-warning systems for water quality and climate monitoring, leaving farmers to react to visible losses rather than anticipate them. This paper reviews the current state of Bihar's three major blue food systems, their production trends, climatic and environmental requirements, and value chain challenges. The paper then presents Twingills, an AI-powered digital twin platform built on NatureDots' AquaNurch Foundation Model, as a proposed intelligence layer to close this gap through real-time and predictive intelligence at farm and landscape scales, forecasting, and timely decision support for farmers and other stakeholders.

items.title: Development and Characterization of Chitosan and Alginate Films Containing Kraft and Organosolv Lignin Nanoparticles for Active Food Packaging
items.authors: Justyna Jakubska, Abdullah, Wojciech Pakieła, K. Gołombek, T. Warski, L. Hawełek
items.abstract: This study examines the effects of kraft and organosolv lignin nanoparticles on chitosan- and sodium alginate-based films designed for active food packaging. Glycerol-plasticized films containing chestnut extract and different nanolignin concentrations were evaluated for their properties and activities. Alginate films generally showed higher tensile strength, reaching 109.35 MPa with 0.2 g of kraft nanolignin, whereas chitosan films provided a better water-vapor barrier, with a minimum permeability of 0.031 mg·µm·Pa−1·s−1·m−2 at 0.02 g of kraft nanolignin. Kraft nanolignin exhibited smaller characteristic structures and produced finer surface features. Organosolv nanolignin formed larger aggregates and generally reduced water absorption. All films decreased light transmission and exhibited antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, with kraft-containing formulations showing the strongest overall inhibition. Spectroscopic, structural, and thermal analyses confirmed intermolecular interactions and slightly improved thermal stability after nanolignin incorporation. All formulations underwent hydrolytic mass loss in phosphate-buffered saline. These findings demonstrate that the matrix, nanolignin type, and concentration can be selected to tailor film properties for specific food-packaging applications.

items.title: Comparative Genomic Insights into Pathogenicity of Diaporthe amygdali and D. eres Associated with Pear Canker in Korea
items.authors: H. Noh, K. Lee, Seong Hwan Kim
items.abstract: Diaporthe species are important fungal pathogens associated with canker and dieback diseases of woody plants, but genomic factors underlying differences in pathogenicity among pear-associated species remain poorly understood. In this study, D. amygdali DUCC20226 and D. eres DUCC15256 were isolated from canker-affected Asian pear (Pyrus pyrifolia) in Korea, representing the first reports of both species causing pear canker in the country. Pathogenicity assays showed that both isolates caused disease symptoms on pear seedlings. High-quality genome assemblies were generated for D. amygdali (49.82 Mb) and D. eres (61.16 Mb), with BUSCO completeness of 98.9% and 98.7%, respectively. Comparative genomic analysis revealed substantial genomic conservation, although strain-specific genes included predicted secreted proteins and candidate effectors. In D. amygdali, two strain-specific candidate effectors potentially associated with necrosis induction were identified. In contrast, D. eres was predicted to possess more carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes, 961 vs. 863) and biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs, 116 vs. 87) than D. amygdali. Mitochondrial genomes differed markedly in size, measuring 49,922 bp in D. amygdali and 93,346 bp in D. eres, despite conserved core gene composition. Phylogenetic analysis based on 15 mitochondrial protein-coding genes placed both strains within Diaporthaceae. These results provide genomic resources for pear-associated Diaporthe species and insights into potential genetic factors underlying pathogenic specialization.

items.title: Actinidia arguta: Organ-Specific Phytochemistry and Biotechnological Applications—A Review
items.authors: G. Melyan, Piotr Latocha, N. Sahakyan
items.abstract: Actinidia arguta Miq., commonly known as kiwiberry or hardy kiwifruit, is increasingly recognized as a multifunctional horticultural species with nutritional, phytochemical, and biotechnological value. Although research has traditionally focused on fruit quality, increasing evidence indicates that leaves, shoots, stems, roots, flowers, seeds, and processing residues contain diverse metabolites with potential applications in food, nutraceuticals, and biomass valorization. This review provides an integrated, organ-oriented analysis of the phytochemical composition, metabolic specialization, molecular regulation, biotechnological potential, and translational applications of A. arguta. Fruits are important sources of vitamin C, soluble sugars, organic acids, dietary fiber, actinidin, and polyphenols, whereas vegetative tissues accumulate phenolics, flavonoids, hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives, and pentacyclic triterpenoids. Seeds represent a lipid-rich compartment characterized by polyunsaturated fatty acids, particularly α-linolenic acid, as well as tocopherols and other lipophilic compounds. Floral tissues contribute diverse volatile metabolites, while processing residues provide additional sources of dietary fiber and bioactive compounds. Recent metabolomic, transcriptomic, and molecular studies reveal substantial effects of genotype, organ identity, developmental stage, and environmental conditions on phytochemical variation. Despite substantial progress, important gaps remain in multi-organ metabolomic characterization, standardization, bioavailability, safety assessment, and clinical validation. Overall, A. arguta can be considered a whole-plant resource with applications spanning functional foods, nutraceuticals, biotechnology, and sustainable biomass valorization.

items.title: Role of Solvent Polarity in the Extraction and Electrochemical Behavior of Antioxidants From <i>Ziziphus jujuba</i> Leaves.
items.authors: Kalsoom U, Hussain Z, Khan S, Ahmad N, Azizi S, Maaza M.
items.abstract: Ziziphus jujuba is a medicinal plant known for its rich content of antioxidants including flavonoids, saponins, phenolics, and triterpenoids. This study determines the effect of solvent polarity on the extraction yield and investigates phytochemical distribution of the extracts and its electrochemical behavior. Reflux extraction was used for the preparation of crude extracts, using methanol, ethanol, and water. The ethanolic extract was selected for solvent fractionation, using n-hexane, dichloromethane, chloroform, and ethyl acetate. Among the extraction solvents, ethanol produced the highest crude yield (6.0% w/w). Following solvent-solvent fractionation, the ethyl acetate fraction showed the highest recovery among all fractions (0.30% w/w). The presence of flavonoid and saponin fractions was confirmed by phytochemical screening. The highest absorbance was observed in ethyl acetate fraction through UV visible spectrophotometric analysis, A = 0.711 for flavonoids at 415 nm and 0.330 for saponin at 406 nm. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) for ethyl acetate and chloroform fractions showed oxidation peaks at 0.50 V (vs. Ag/AgCl). Fourier transformed infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) analyzed functional groups of flavonoids and saponins. Liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS) identified major flavonoids, that is, vicenin II, spinosin, kaemferol (glycoside), and saponins (jujubosides). The result stated that the polarity of solvents plays a vital role in extracting redox-active antioxidants from the leaves of Z. jujuba. Furthermore, it stated that ethyl acetate is the most effective fractionation solvent. This study gives analytical framework for extraction and characterization of antioxidant-rich fraction of Z. jujuba leaves along with emphasis on the role of solvent polarity …

items.title: Antibacterial properties of commercially available plant extracts containing tannins against Escherichia coli
items.authors: Ewa Olchowik-Grabarek, Szymon Sekowski
items.abstract: Escherichia coli is a gram-negative bacterium that exists as commensal microorganism and can diversify into pathogenic strains that cause illnesses in humans and animals. Whilst antibiotics are the most commonly used compounds against E.coli , many other compounds, such as polyphenols, demonstrate strong antibacterial activity. In this work, the antibacterial potential of five commercially available plant compounds: chestnut extract, mimosa extract, quebracho extract, ellagic acid and gallic acid against E.coli was investigated. In the studies, standard microbiological tests, including MIC (minimal inhibitory concentration) and MBC (minimum bactericidal concentration), were performed. Also, to better study and explain the antibacterial potential of analyzed compounds against E.coli , additional investigations involving cell membrane fluidity analyses, Zeta potential measurements, and activity against hemolysis induced by E.coli toxins has been conducted. Our results demonstrated that all five compounds have antibacterial activity, but the strongest activity is observed for ellagic acid and chestnut. Investigated compounds possess the potential to modulate E.coli membrane fluidity and to inhibit the sheep erythrocytes hemolysis evoked by E.coli toxin.

items.title: Transcriptome profiling reveals AGAMOUS-LIKE genes associated with the reprogramming of mature endosperm cell fate in hardy kiwifruit
items.authors: Malec J, Dutkiewicz Z, Trościński JK, Popielarska-Konieczna M, Czernicka M.
items.abstract: Abstract Background Mature endosperm is a highly differentiated storage tissue with limited capacity for developmental reprogramming. Although in vitro culture can induce endosperm dedifferentiation and regeneration in hardy kiwifruit ( Actinidia arguta ), the transcriptional changes associated with this transition remain poorly understood. This study investigated early reprogramming of mature endosperm in two cultivars with contrasting culture responses, focusing on AGAMOUS-LIKE ( AGL ) transcription factors. Methods RNA sequencing was performed on freshly isolated endosperm and explants cultured for 14 days on thidiazuron-containing medium from cultivars 'Bingo' and 'Weiki', with three biological replicates per condition. De novo transcriptome assembly was followed by functional annotation, differential expression analysis and GO and KEGG enrichment analyses. Selected AGL candidates were further characterised using sequence alignment, conserved-domain analysis, maximum-likelihood phylogenetic reconstruction and three-dimensional protein modelling. Results The assembly yielded 149,380 unigenes. Comparisons between cultured and freshly isolated endosperm identified 29,814 differentially expressed genes in 'Bingo' and 35,893 in 'Weiki', with 21,365 shared between the two comparisons. Culture-associated transcriptional changes involved ribosome biogenesis, protein synthesis, cell wall organisation, transport and carbohydrate and lipid metabolism. AP2/EREBP , WRKY and MYB transcription factors exhibited shared induction patterns alongside cultivar-dependent responses in additional regulatory families. items.title: Antibacterial Effect of Extracts Rich in Tannins Isolated from Berry Waste Against Pathogens Contaminating Food
items.authors: Hejduk A, Piekarska–Radzik L, Sójka M, Klewicki R, Ścieszka S, Klewicka E.
items.abstract: Background: Microbiological contamination of food and the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance have intensified the search for natural alternatives to conventional preservatives. Berry-processing pomace is a rich source of tannins with recognized antimicrobial potential; however, information on the relationship between tannin composition and activity against foodborne pathogens remains limited. Methods and results: Tannin-rich extracts were isolated from pomace obtained after the processing of raspberry and blackberry (Rubus) as well as strawberry and wild strawberry (Fragaria) fruits using acetone extraction followed by purification with Amberlite XAD 1600 N resin and Size Exclusion Chromatography. The composition of the extracts was characterized by HPLC-DAD-MS QExactive and HPLC-FD. Antibacterial activity against 15 foodborne pathogenic strains belonging to the genera Listeria, Escherichia, Salmonella, and Staphylococcus was evaluated using disk diffusion and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) assays, while antibiofilm activity was assessed against Listeria innocua. Eight extracts differing in ellagitannin (10-72 g/100 g) and condensed tannin (4-25 g/100 g) contents were evaluated. All extracts exhibited antibacterial activity, and inhibition zones were positively correlated with ellagitannin content and negatively correlated with procyanidin concentration. For most microorganisms, MIC values ranged from 0.391 to 12.5 mg/mL, with no significant differences between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, whereas the susceptibility of Listeria monocytogenes depended on the strain and extract type. Furthermore, all extracts significantly reduced L. innocua biofilm formation. Conclusions: Tannin-rich extracts recovered from berry-processing by-products…

items.title: Eco-friendly synthesis of ZnO-PVA nanoparticles using Diospyros kaki fruit extract and its antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against Streptococcus mutans.
items.journal: Odontology : official journal of The Society of the Nippon Dental University
items.authors: Venkatesan KB, Pathallapalli A, Packirisamy V, Srinivasan MK.
items.abstract: Dental caries is a major global oral health concern primarily associated with Streptococcus mutans biofilm formation, which exhibits considerable resistance to conventional antimicrobial therapies. This study aimed to synthesize and evaluate green-fabricated zinc oxide-polyvinyl alcohol nanoparticles (ZnO-PVA NPs) mediated by Diospyros kaki fruit extract for antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against S. mutans. ZnO-PVA NPs were synthesized using an aqueous fruit extract of D. kaki. Phytochemicals, including polyphenols and flavonoids, have been reported in D. kaki extracts and may contribute to the reduction and stabilization processes during nanoparticle synthesis. The synthesized NPs were characterized using UV-visible spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering (DLS), and zeta potential analysis. Antibacterial efficacy was evaluated by determining the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), while antibiofilm potential was assessed using confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). Characterization analyses confirmed the successful synthesis of crystalline ZnO NPs dispersed within an amorphous PVA matrix. The NPs exhibited an average hydrodynamic size of 169.41 nm and a zeta potential of - 31.03 mV, indicating high colloidal stability. Antibacterial evaluation demonstrated dose-dependent inhibition of S. mutans, with an MIC value of 31.25 µg/mL. CLSM analysis further revealed substantial disruption of mature biofilms, confirming both antibacterial and antibiofilm properties. items.title: AaF3'5'H involved in flavonoid synthesis in hairy roots of Actinidia arguta (Siebold & Zucc.) Planch. ex Miq.
items.authors: Jiang Y, Xiao Y, Han H, Bai Y, Ma L, Li J, Ji X, Lei P, Meng F.
items.abstract: The kiwifruit (Actinidia arguta) is rich in diverse bioactive compounds, particularly flavonoids, which exhibit potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-tumor properties. Flavonoid 3'5'-hydroxylase (F3'5'H) is a key enzyme in the synthesis pathway of flavonoids. However, the functional role of the AaF3'5'H gene in A. arguta remains poorly understood. In this study, the AaF3'5'H gene was cloned. Its coding sequence (CDS) is 1344 bp in length, encoding a 447-amino-acid protein localized to the cytoplasm. Overexpression of AaF3'5'H significantly increased the flavonoid content in transgenic Arabidopsis and promoted growth and development. VIGS-mediated silencing of AaF3'5'H in A. arguta significantly reduced flavonoid accumulation and suppressed plant growth. In contrast, overexpression of AaF3'5'H in transgenic hairy roots enhanced root morphogenesis and significantly elevated total flavonoid content. Targeted metabolomics analysis further revealed 50 differentially expressed metabolites, among which 24 are upregulated and 26 are downregulated. KEGG pathway enrichment and metabolic mapping revealed that these differentially expressed metabolites were predominantly involved in flavonoid biosynthesis, flavone and flavonol biosynthesis, and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis. In conclusion, this study confirms that the AaF3'5'H gene plays a crucial role in positively regulating the biosynthesis of flavonoids and promoting the formation of root morphology. This provides a theoretical basis for the variety improvement of A. arguta and the utilization of flavonoid resources.

items.title: Fermentation characteristics and gut microbiota modulation of pectic polysaccharides from jujube: The critical role of degree of esterification and branching.
items.authors: Liu W, Zhang Z, Yuan Q, Xia Y, Huang J, Zhong J, Wang S, Chen X, Wu D.
items.abstract: Microbiota preference for pectic polysaccharides depends on degree of esterification (DE) and degree of branching (DB), which in turn shapes microbial composition and metabolite production. Here, four jujube polysaccharides were prepared and characterized, including the original polysaccharide (JP), the modified polysaccharide with a low DE (JP-LDE), and the modified polysaccharide with a medium or low DB (JP-MDB or JP-LDB). During in vitro fecal fermentation, JP-LDE, JP-MDB, and JP-LDB were utilized more rapidly and completely than JP, withtotal fermentability increased from 56.34% (JP) to 76.58% (JP-LDB). Gut microbiota composition differed significantly among groups depending on DE and DB. Compared with JP, JP-LDE modulated the increased relative abundance of Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum, Megasphaera elsdenii, and Anthropogastromicrobium aceti, while JP-MDB and JP-LDBpredominantly increased the relative abundance of Megasphaera elsdenii and Anthropogastromicrobium aceti. These microbial shifts markedly increased short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production, particularly butyric acid. Our findings provide new insights into pectic polysaccharide structure-activity relationships during human fecal fermentation.

items.title: Removal of the antidepressant flupentixol from aqueous solution using jujube oil-based emulsion liquid membrane through hybrid optimization of RSM and ANN
items.authors: B. Kuppusamy, Sivarajasekar Natesan, Ramalingam Ramamoorthy, V. P. Sundramurthy, Kibebe Sahele
items.abstract: Recently, membrane-based separation gains significant attention among available water treatment technologies. Among the advanced techniques for wastewater treatment, emulsion liquid membranes (ELM) stand out, since it is environmentally friendly. In the present work, flupentixol (FL), an emergent micropollutant and antidepressant, was selected as the model pharmaceutical pollutant for removal using ELM system containing jujube oil (JJO-ELM). The primary effects and interactions of key independent variables, surfactant concentration (2–3 v/v %), carrier concentration (3–5 v/v %), concentration of stripping agent (HCl), (0.5–1.5 N), FL concentration (50–150 mg/L), and phase ratio (1:1–1:3 for water:JJO, respectively) were optimized using the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) design components. Optimized results showed that the ideal condition for the independent parameters, surfactant concentration; carrier concentration, HCl concentration, flupentixol concentration, and a phase ratio, respectively, were determined to be 2.41% v/v, 3.70% v/v, 0.52 N, 143.84 mg/L, and 1:1.5. The ideal condition could result in a maximum extraction efficiency of 97.40% FL. Further, the effectiveness of FL stripping was examined by adjusting the H2SO4 concentration. Investigations were made into the mechanism of flupentixol extraction by JJO-ELM. The feed forward neural network (FNN) model, which has an output layer with one (flupentixol extraction) neuron and an input layer with five neurons, was used to simulate the extraction data. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

items.title: Different Formulations and Concentrations of Sweet Chestnut Tannins Differentially Modulate Gut Microbiota in Broiler Chickens
items.authors: Isidora Prošić, M. Brus, Nikola Delić, N. Zdravković, A. Radalj, Tamaš Petrović
items.abstract: Sweet chestnut tannins (SCT) are used as phytogenic feed additives in poultry, but the effects of different formulations and concentrations on intestinal microbiota remain poorly understood. This study investigated powdered, soy protein-bound, microencapsulated and orthophosphoric acid-bound SCT at different dietary concentrations in sixty Ross 308 broilers, with six birds per group, including an unsupplemented control. Ileal and caecal microbiota were characterized using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. In the ileum, richness, phylogenetic diversity and beta diversity differed among treatments, whereas Shannon diversity and evenness remained unchanged. Lactobacillaceae remained dominant, and no significant family- or genus-level differences relative to the control remained after multiple-testing correction. In the caecum, all assessed alpha- and beta-diversity metrics differed among treatments, with numerous treatment-specific taxonomic changes. Several treatments increased the Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio, while Muribaculaceae decreased across most supplemented groups. Soy protein-bound SCT at 1000 mg/kg increased Parabacteroides and Odoribacter, whereas microencapsulated SCT at 1000 mg/kg increased Romboutsia and Peptostreptococcaceae. The genus Fournierella increased with soy protein-bound SCT at 2000 mg/kg. Responses were not consistently dose-dependent. These findings indicate that SCT-associated microbial changes vary with intestinal compartment, formulation and concentration, with broader responses detected in the caecum. Their implications for bird health and performance require further investigation.

items.title: Evolutionary dynamics of the pan-centromere architecture in oaks
items.authors: Lin Q, Liang Y, Yan W, Run Y, You H, Zhou B, Ling S, Shen Z, Wang J, Niu J, Luo W, Qiao L, Shan S, Elshaer L, Tucker A, Feng C, Shi Y, Mohn R, Liang Y, Zhang N, Liu X, Hipp A, Manos PS, Cavender-Bares
items.abstract: Centromeres ensure faithful chromosome segregation and genome stability, yet their DNA evolves rapidly, presenting a long-standing centromere paradox. Here we characterise the genomic and epigenomic architecture of >1,300 candidate centromeres from 111 high-quality Quercus (oak) genomes. We show that lineage-specific expansion of QuCEN146 satellite drives centromere turnover in oaks by displacing ancestral LTR-rich sequences into flanking regions, with genetic drift facilitating fixation of satellite-rich centromeres. Population-scale analyses in Q. serrata reveal extensive variation in satellite rich centromeres, generated by array expansion and contraction, strand-orientation shifts, and interspecific introgression. By contrast, LTR rich centromeres of Q. variabilis exhibit extremely low polymorphism and high collinearity across populations, sustained by suppressed local recombination, linked selection, and constrained LTR dynamics. We further demonstrate chromosome-independent evolutionary patterns for both satellite-rich and LTR-rich centromeres. Collectively, these findings demonstrate how evolutionary processes drive centromere turnover and shape contrasting centromeric sequence landscapes in forest trees.

items.title: Adaptive Genomic Variation Across Sub-Alpine Climates in a Keystone Forest Tree: Implications for Seed Sourcing for Restoration in a Changing Climate.
items.authors: Whale JW, Stuart KC, Bruce J, Pickup M, Field DL.
items.abstract: A major challenge for ecological restoration is seed sourcing decisions that ensure that restored populations have the adaptive variation for current and future environments. This is increasingly important for alpine and sub-alpine communities where climate change is predicted to be rapid and drive shifts in selective pressures. Selecting source populations representing future climates is an evolutionary-based strategy for increasing adaptive capacity, but requires an understanding of population genetic structure, identification of putatively adaptive genomic variation and an assessment of how these change across the landscape. Using 3978 single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers we assessed the population structure and diversity of 33 sampled populations of Eucalyptus delegatensis from across its distribution, including 22 populations from the mainland ( E. delegatensis subsp. delegatensis ) and 11 from Tasmania ( E. delegatensis subsp. tasmaniensis ). Genotype-environment association (GEA) analysis identified strong genetic associations with seasonal climate variables, particularly minimum temperature of the coldest month, and revealed a parallel cline at one outlier locus across the mainland and Tasmanian range, consistent with independent sorting of standing variation along environmental gradients in both subspecies. By projecting genetic offset under future climate change scenarios, we identify regions of the species' range most vulnerable to projected change; despite this, seed-sourcing projections suggest that suitable future climate matches may be available for most of the range. Together, these findings demonstrate the value of comparative GEA approaches in validating outlier loci, and show that even in regions of projected dramatic environmental shifts, suc…

items.title: Enhancing flavor, antioxidant activity, and bitterness improvement in chestnut-Cistanche co-fermentation: a sensomics and widely targeted metabolomics study.
items.authors: Cui R, Xiao Y, Huai L, Li J, Wang X, Yao Y, Wang H, Zhang Y, Song L.
items.abstract: Our study developed a chestnut-Cistanche co-fermented beverage (CCFB) using mixed lactic acid bacteria (LAB) fermentation. The quality of different types of CCFB were studied. Firstly, LAB fermentation significantly altered the physicochemical properties, flavor, and taste of CCFB using Lactobacillus plantarum LWCC3001 and Lactobacillus plantarum LWCC3005. Fermentation enhanced antioxidant activity, with the ABTS radical scavenging rate doubling. Secondly, electronic tongue analysis showed the bitterness response signal value of the ZW3005 group (1.50) was significantly lower than CK (0.02) (P < 0.05). GC-IMS detected 27 volatile compounds. Among them, propanal decreased approximately 12-fold in the mixed fermentation (MIX) group. Comprehensive metabolomics analysis revealed that fermentation substantially reshaped the metabolic profiles of the CCFB. Specifically, the alkaloid metabolism pathway promoted the degradation of certain bitter compounds, while activation of the phenylpropanoid metabolism pathway enhanced the biosynthesis of antioxidant compounds. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the further processing of CCFB.

items.title: Watering and Leaf Removal as Strategies to Mitigate Cameraria ohridella Damage in Urban Horse Chestnuts
items.authors: Ivan Iľko, M. Raček, V. Peterková, Martin Hurban
items.abstract: Removal of infested leaf litter reduces overwintering Cameraria ohridella populations. Whether supplemental irrigation combined with removal can alleviate drought stress and improve the condition of infested urban horse chestnuts remains insufficiently evaluated. This quasi-experimental study compared treatments applied at 7 sites: untreated control (no leaf removal or irrigation); removal alone; removal plus rainfall-adjusted irrigation of 2 m 3 to 4 m 3 tree −1 every 14 days (regular); removal plus automated irrigation of 70 mm month −1 during April to September (enhanced); and two foliar sprays of the contact insecticide lambda-cyhalothrin at one site. Sampling occurred each September in 2020 and 2021 but only in 2020 at the insecticide site. Leaf-miner damage, total leaf area, dry mass, and estimated specific leaf area were analyzed as tree level means. Median tree level damage was approximately 91% at the control and 85% after leaf removal alone (not significantly different) compared with 48% to 69% at regular-irrigation sites and 11% to 44% at enhanced-irrigation sites. Site 6 (L6), comprising solitary trees under leaf removal and enhanced irrigation, had the lowest damage, with leaf area and dry mass among the highest. At the insecticide site, median damaged leaf area was approximately 42% for lower-canopy samples and 75% for upper-canopy samples. Estimated specific leaf area did not differ among sites. Combined leaf removal and irrigation were associated with lower damage and better leaf condition, particularly at L6. These site-level associations support the combined strategy as a host-condition intervention without isolating irrigation’s contribution or demonstrating direct pest suppression. L6 had numerically less damage than both insecticide-treated canopy p…

items.title: Tannin Phenology is Associated with the Timing of Asiatic Black Bear Foraging among Persimmon Fruit Types
items.authors: D. Fujiki
items.abstract: This study examined whether variation in tannin concentrations and tannin insolubilization timing among persimmon fruit types influences foraging frequency and seasonal timing in Asiatic black bears (Ursus thibetanus). Bear-constructed feeding platforms in persimmon trees served as fruit consumption indicators. The probability of platform formation was highest in pollination-constant nonastringent (PCNA) persimmons, intermediate in pollination-variant nonastringent (PVNA) fruit, and lower in pollination-variant astringent (PVA) and pollination-constant astringent (PCA) types. Platform formation timing followed a similar sequence, occurring earliest in PCNA, then PVNA, and subsequently PVA and PCA persimmons. Soluble phenolic content, a proxy for tannin concentration, was measured in fruit collected immediately after platform formation. Bear feeding platform formation was observed mainly at relatively low soluble phenolic levels, generally below approximately 0.5% fresh weight (FW) tannic acid equivalents (TAE). Generalized additive models describing seasonal changes in soluble phenolic concentrations indicated that concentrations were highest in PCA, followed by PVA, PVNA, and PCNA persimmons. The decline to low concentrations occurred earliest in PCNA and progressively later through PVNA, PVA, and PCA types. Overall, these findings suggest that soluble phenolic concentration and its seasonal dynamics may be associated with the temporal patterns of bear foraging on persimmon fruit.

items.title: New insights into the adaptive chloroplast capture in European white oaks
items.authors: Sergiadou D, Wood D, Dunning LT, Kjaer ED, Olofsson JK.
items.abstract: Abstract Chloroplast genomes are frequently used to reconstruct the evolutionary history of plants, including detection of introgression and chloroplast capture events. Here, we focus on two oak species, Quercus robur and Q. petraea , which lack differentiation in several chloroplast markers. This was assumed to result from chloroplast captures during their dispersal from refugia after the last glacial maximum (LGM). We aim to reassess chloroplast variation within and between these species by de novo assembling 114 oak plastomes. Additionally, we combine our data with available plastome data from 91 Fagaceae species to reconstruct a dated phylogeny and estimate the divergence time between oak chloroplast lineages. Positive selection analysis on 69 chloroplast genes was also conducted to test whether chloroplast capture is adaptive. Plastome phylogenetic analyses reveal three oak haplotypes with no species delimitation. Molecular dating analysis indicates older splits among the three main haplotypes (2.68 − 0.5 Mya) and younger splits within lineages (0.39 − 0.04 Mya), suggesting that chloroplast capture could have occurred prior to the LGM in some lineages. Positive selection is observed in two chloroplast genes, with the selection on the rbcL gene possibly linked to the adaptive evolution of the RuBisCO enzyme. Hence, signs of a selective sweep could further explain the observed limited genetic diversity in oak plastomes. This study provides valuable insights into oak plastome evolution, setting a significant base for upcoming studies, including nuclear genome and protein-level studies to better understand cytonuclear interactions and conceivable environmental adaptations.

items.title: Identification of key chestnut-sweet aroma compounds in bud-leaf yellow tea and analysis of their dynamic changes and formation mechanism.
items.authors: Zhou J, Bi L, Shu Q, Zhang X, Jia T, Zhang, Ni D, Yu Z.
items.abstract: Bud-leaf yellow tea is known for its chestnut-sweet aroma, yet its key odorants and formation mechanism remain unclear. Using a sensomics approach, seven key odorants were characterized, including 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine, 3-methylbutanal, and dimethyl sulfide, with 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine being the major contributor (recombination correlation r = 0.909). 2-Ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine (odor activity value = 53.3, flavor dilution = 1024) and dimethyl sulfide (odor activity value = 422.4, flavor dilution = 256) were identified as major contributors, with dimethyl sulfide dominating the chestnut note and 2-Ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine enhancing the sweet dimension. Across Meizhan, FudingDabaicha and Echa 10, 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine was undetectable before yellowing, peaked during yellowing (14.92 μg/L, p < 0.05), and was moisture-dependent, with 25% post-fixation moisture giving the highest chestnut-sweet score. In vitro, β-alanine + D-arabinose produced 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine via the Maillard reaction. Thus, 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine is the yellowing-specific key chestnut-sweet odorant in bud-leaf yellow tea, enabling moisture-based process control.

items.title: Chestnut starch-lipid complex as a nontraditional RS5 ingredient: Structural features and associated in vivo responses in high-fat diet-fed mice.
items.authors: Yu Z, Ma N, Wei F, Deng J, Cui H, Lv H, Ji X, Lu Y, Wang S.
items.abstract: Resistant starch type 5 (RS5) can convert starch-rich crops into enzyme-resistant starch-lipid complexes, yet current evidence remains dominated by conventional starch sources and in vitro studies. This study prepared and characterized a chestnut starch-stearic acid complex (chestnut starch-lipid complex, DCS_C18, RS5), and evaluated it as a novel RS5 ingredient in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice, using native chestnut starch, caffeine, and orlistat as contextual comparators. DCS_C18 showed V-/B-type crystalline features, greater short-range and long-range order, and higher thermal stability than the palmitic acid complex. In vivo, DCS_C18 attenuated HFD-induced weight gain, adiposity, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, hepatic steatosis, and systemic inflammation, accompanied by reduced lipogenic and increased fatty acid oxidation-related gene expression. Moreover, DCS_C18 exhibited more balanced regulation of fasting and postprandial glycemia than the other interventions. DCS_C18 also increased fecal acetate (2.12-fold) and butyrate (1.82-fold) and enriched SCFA-associated genera, including Blautia, Roseburia, and Lachnoclostridium. Open-field testing suggested improved locomotor and anxiety-related outcomes without the stimulant-like pattern observed for caffeine. These findings support chestnut-derived RS5 as a promising ingredient platform for metabolic-health-oriented foods, pending human and mechanistic confirmation.

items.title: Windthrow of Forest Trees and Its Effect on Tree Regeneration and Diversity of Understory in the Hyrcanian Temperate Upland Forests of Iran
items.authors: B. Kiani, Sharare Behbudi, Mehrdad Nikooy, A. Omidi
items.abstract: Windthrow is a major natural disturbance shaping canopy dynamics in temperate forests, yet high-elevation (upland) Hyrcanian forests remain poorly studied, particularly with respect to regeneration responses and topographic controls. This study examined windfall effects in Dashte Daman forests, northern Iran (1027–1629 m elevation). First, 90 systematically distributed 50 × 50 m sample plots were established across a 300 × 300 m grid on a stratified map including affected and unaffected areas. For each fallen tree (broken or uprooted), diameter at breast height, trunk height, and crown length were measured. Understory vegetation composition, including herbaceous cover and tree regeneration, was also recorded. The influence of topographic variables (slope, elevation, aspect) and forest type on windfall abundance was analyzed, alongside correlations with slope, elevation, distance to nearest road, stand density, and canopy cover. Comparisons with undisturbed control areas were made to assess regeneration patterns. Results indicated that oriental beech (Fagus orientalis) was the most windfall species, followed by common hornbeam (Carpinus betulus), whereas chestnut-leaved oak (Quercus castaneifolia) and common ash (Fraxinus excelsior) were rare. Windfall frequency averaged eight fallen and 4.7 uprooted (a total of 12.7) trees per hectare, with corresponding volumes of 31.6 m3/ha and 18.56 m3/ha, respectively. Considering the abundance of wind-fallen trees, windfall frequency was highest on south-, southwest-, and west-aspects, at slopes of 20%–40%, and elevations of 1000–1200 m. Valleys exhibited greater tree breakage, whereas uprooting dominated hillsides. Pure oriental beech stands had significantly higher windfall rates than mixed beech-hornbeam or oak-hornbeam forests.…

items.title: Pear Peel-Enriched Residue Extract Attenuates Ethanol-Induced Liver Injury Through Regulation of Antioxidant Signaling and Lipid Metabolism.
items.authors: Thakuri LS, Le D, Sonar NS, Park HB, Subedi L, Lee KS, Shon JH, Park JW, Lee M, Rhyu DY.
items.abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption induces progressive liver injury through oxidative stress, lipid accumulation, and inflammation, primarily driven by dysregulated ethanol (EtOH) metabolism. Given the growing interest in plant-derived phytochemicals for hepatoprotection, pear ( Pyrus pyrifolia ) has attracted attention due to its antioxidant and lipid-regulating properties; however, the bioactive fractions and mechanisms underlying the hepatoprotective effects of pear peel-enriched residue extracts (PPE) remain unclear. Therefore, we evaluated the hepatoprotective potential of PPE against EtOH-induced liver injury using in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. In HepG2 cells, PPE reduced oxidative stress, restored cell viability, and reduced intracellular EtOH and acetaldehyde levels more effectively than pear extract, with efficacy comparable to silymarin. In EtOH-treated C57BL/6 mice, PPE attenuated liver injury markers, reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, and improved histopathological alterations. PPE also modulated the expression of proteins associated with oxidative stress and lipid metabolism. GNPS-FBMN analysis putatively annotated over 120 phytochemicals (or metabolites), and in silico analyses suggested potential interactions between selected metabolites and proteins involved in EtOH metabolism and lipid regulation. These findings suggest that PPE shows hepatoprotective potential and warrants further investigation as a potential candidate for the mitigation of alcohol-associated liver disease.

items.title: Jujuboside A ameliorates T2DM-associated MASH: Suppression of YY1/FAS axis-mediated hepatic de novo fatty acid biosynthesis.
items.authors: Yang T, Chen L, Luo H, Wang L, Jiang X, Yang H, Chen L, Qian S, Wang T, Li B, Ji F, Yan X, Yin X, Lu Q.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represents a progressive subtype of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and is predominantly driven by dysregulated hepatic fatty acid (FA) metabolism. Although Jujuboside A (Ju A), a major bioactive triterpene saponin isolated from Ziziphus jujuba Mill. (sour jujube), exhibits hepatoprotective properties, its precise regulatory mechanisms underlying T2DM-associated MASH remain poorly defined. This study investigated the dose-dependent protective effects and molecular mechanisms of Ju A using both in vivo and in vitro models. Combining targeted FA profiling and long-chain FAs (LCFAs)-specific metabolomics, alongside chromatin immunoprecipitation (Ch-IP), luciferase reporter assays, molecular docking with dynamics simulations, and Yin Yang 1 (YY1) gain-of-function and fatty acid synthase (FAS) inhibition (C75) studies, we characterized Ju A-mediated metabolic reprogramming and molecular targets involved. Ju A treatment markedly ameliorated MASH and hepatic lipid deposition in diabetic mice by restoring dysregulated hepatic FA homeostasis, particularly by blocking de novo lipogenesis (DNL)-derived LCFA accumulation. Mechanistically, Ju A exerted these effects by blocking the nuclear translocation of YY1. This inhibition diminished YY1 binding to the FAS promoter, subsequently downregulating FAS expression and inhibiting aberrant hepatic de novo FA biosynthesis. Collectively, these findings demonstrated that Ju A ameliorated T2DM-associated MASH by restoring hepatic FA homeostasis via inactivation of the YY1-FAS axis, highlighting its promising therapeutic potential against diabetic liver complications.

items.title: Photocatalytic treatment of AO7 and real textile wastewater using green-synthesized ZnO nanoparticles: RSM and Taguchi approach.
items.authors: Turkoglu S, Kepekci RA, Keskinkan O.
items.abstract: In this study, ZnO nanoparticles were synthesized via a green synthesis method using Diospyros kaki L. peel extract, and their photocatalytic performances for the removal of Acid Orange 7 (AO7) dye and real textile wastewater were investigated. The effects of pH, initial dye concentration, and catalyst dosage on AO7 removal were optimized using a Box-Behnken experimental design and Response Surface Methodology (RSM). Under the optimum conditions (pH 10, initial dye concentration of 10 ppm, and catalyst dosage of 0.13 g), 100% dye removal was achieved within 270 min. The photocatalytic treatment of real textile wastewater was optimized using a Taguchi experimental design, and a color removal efficiency of 98.1% was achieved under the optimum conditions (pH 7, constant wastewater volume of 50 mL, and catalyst dosage of 0.13 g). Additionally, radical scavenging experiments performed to elucidate the photocatalytic mechanism indicated that hydroxyl radicals (•OH) play a significant role in the photocatalytic degradation of AO7. The synthesized ZnO nanoparticles exhibited high photocatalytic stability, good reusability and acted as efficient photocatalysts even under low-energy UV light conditions. Overall, the green-synthesized ZnO nanoparticles demonstrated promising potential as an effective photocatalyst for the removal of dyes and color from real textile wastewater.

items.title: From Textile Waste Toward a Leather Alternative: Mechanical and Abrasion Performance of Polycaprolactone-Reinforced Reclaimed Nonwoven Cotton
items.authors: Bahar Hashemian Esfahani, S. Dutta, R. Eike, Boyce S. Chang, Zahra Falsafi, Manu Smriti
items.abstract: Transforming textile waste into durable, value-added materials remains a central challenge for sustainable apparel systems. This study developed single-layer, nonwoven sheets from discarded 100% cotton textiles using a papermaking-derived wet-laid process and evaluated their potential as leather-alternative materials through a sequential two-phase approach. In Phase 1, reclaimed-cotton nonwoven sheets bio-finished with persimmon juice or konjac were benchmarked against commercial plant-based olive, cork, pineapple, and cactus leather alternatives using ASTM grab tensile and rotary-platform abrasion testing. The bio-finished sheets showed low breaking forces, limited elongation, and abrasion failure. In Phase 2, biodegradable polycaprolactone (PCL) was applied as a reinforcing finish. The resulting PCL-treated reclaimed-cotton sheets’ (RC-PCL) breaking force performance improved by over 6.5 times the nontreated nonwoven specimens and approximately 4.5 times the bio-finished nonwoven specimens. Additionally, the RC-PCL completed the 2000-cycle abrasion endpoint without through-thickness failure. Elongation remained low while the dogbone tensile test showed increases in tensile strength, strain at break, and apparent Young’s modulus after PCL-finishing. These findings indicate that biodegradable PCL-finish substantially improves the strength, cohesion, and abrasion resistance of reclaimed-cotton nonwovens, while flexibility, coating optimization, and end-of-life performance remain priorities for future leather-alternative applications to support sustainability efforts and value-added use of reclaimed materials within the textile industry.

items.title: Studies of the Antioxidant Mechanisms Produced by Black Raspberries Extracts (Rubus niveus Thunb) and Magnesium Salt Mixtures in Red Blood Cells

items.title: Fosetyl-Al stem injection for chestnut ink disease management: efficacy and dose-dependent phytotoxicity in saplings
items.authors: P. Serrano-Pérez, G. Moreno, Mikel Cebadero, M. C. Rodríguez-Molina
items.abstract: Fosetyl-Al (aluminium tris-(ethyl phosphonate)) is a low-toxicity phosphonate commonly used to control oomycete-related diseases in crops. Trunk injection (endotherapy) delivers the fungicide directly into the vascular system, potentially improving efficacy while reducing off-target losses. This two-year study evaluated the efficacy and phytotoxicity of stem-injected fosetyl-Al to manage ink disease caused by Phytophthora cinnamomi in Castanea sativa saplings. Fifty saplings received fosetyl-Al injections at 0–4% using pressurized devices, followed by stem inoculation with the pathogen; a 2% soil irrigation treatment was included for comparison. Stem injections at 1%, 2% and 4% significantly suppressed stem necrosis after inoculation with P. cinnamomi and reduced root infections compared to irrigation and untreated control. Protection persisted for at least two years as reflected by reduced relative Area Under the Disease Progress Curve (rAUDPC) values. However, stem injections also induced phytotoxic symptoms, including leaf burn, necrosis, and occasional plant death, with a clear dose-dependent relationship. Most plants recovered from moderate phytotoxicity, whereas irreversible damage occurred at the highest doses, highlighting the critical need for precise dose adjustments, particularly in small-diameter trees. Logistic regression identified a Minimum Effective Dose (MED) range of 0.061–0.102 g/cm (a.i.) of stem circumference, corresponding to predicted disease incidence thresholds of < 10% to < 1%, respectively, with associated phytotoxicity risks of approximately 10–25%. These results indicate that trunk injection of fosetyl-Al can provide effective and targeted control of ink disease in young chestnut plants under the conditions tested, while emphasizing the need…

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Physicochemical Properties, Bioactive Compounds and Chemometric Discrimination of Honey Samples from Different Botanical and Geographical Origins
items.authors: Arleta Rifati-Nixha, M. Dërmaku-Sopjani, Mustafa Arslan, Edlira Riza, Ariona Lubishtani
items.abstract: The chemical and quality characteristics of honey vary considerably according to floral source, geographical provenance, environmental conditions, and post-harvest handling, complicating its characterization and authentication. In this study, physicochemical properties, bioactive constituents, enzymatic activity, and exploratory chemometric patterns were evaluated in thirteen honey samples representing different declared botanical types, including sage, meadow, chestnut, acacia, and pine honeys, from different geographical origins. Physicochemical characterization comprised moisture content, refractive index, specific optical rotation, electrical conductivity, pH, free acidity, hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), reducing sugars, ash content, qualitative mineral composition, and preliminary authenticity-related tests. Total phenolic content determined by the Folin–Ciocalteu assay (TPC-FC), total flavonoid content (TFC), total phenolic content determined by the Prussian Blue assay (TPC-PB), proline content, and diastase activity were also evaluated. Statistical analysis included one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by Tukey’s HSD test, Pearson correlation analysis, and principal component analysis (PCA). One-way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD test indicated significant differences in the measured analytical responses among the individual honey samples for the evaluated bioactive parameters (p < 0.05); these comparisons were restricted to the investigated samples and were not interpreted as inferential differences among botanical or geographical populations. Pearson correlation analysis revealed several moderate-to-strong associations among the analytical variables; however, none remained statistically significant after Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) corre…

items.title: Accumulation of two distinct alleles causes astringency loss in cultivated polyploid persimmon
items.authors: Fujiwara Y, Nishiyama S, Onoue N, Matsuzaki R, Kono A, Azuma A, Saito T, Shimizu T, Sato A, Ichino T, Yamane H, Yonemori K, Tao R.
items.abstract: Persimmon fruit accumulates high levels of proanthocyanidins (PAs), causing extreme astringency. In pollination-constant and non-astringent (PCNA) cultivars, PA accumulation ceases early in fruit development. Although the PCNA trait is recessively controlled by the ASTRINGENCY ( AST ) locus, its causal gene has remained unknown. Using haplotype-resolved forward genetics in a hexaploid genetic background, we identified the previously uncharacterized TANNIN ( TAN ) as the causal gene. Long-read sequencing revealed that PCNA originated through the accumulation of independently derived ast alleles that cause transcriptional deficiency of TAN . These findings resolve the complex genetic basis of natural astringency loss in persimmon and provide a framework for molecular breeding. Further investigation of TAN function would uncover mechanisms underlying massive accumulation of PAs in persimmon fruit and insight into specialized metabolite sequestration.

items.title: Adding Geographical Indication Protection to a Regional Collective Trademark: Evidence on Rural Production and Commercialisation in Japan
items.authors: Matsui K.
items.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether Geographical Indication (GI) registration generates additional changes in rural production and commercialisation when a regional product is already protected by a Regional Collective Trademark (RCT). Using Ichida Gaki, a traditional dried persimmon from Nagano Prefecture, Japan, as a case, the study compares the RCT-only period (2007–2015) with the combined RCT-plus-GI period (2017–2023). A prefecture-year panel is analysed using two-way fixed-effects models, event-study analyses, and spatial analyses. Relative to comparison prefectures, production volume remained comparatively higher after GI registration, while shipment volume and shipment rate declined. The decline in shipment volume received the strongest empirical support and remained robust across alternative specifications, whereas pre-treatment trends limit causal interpretation for production volume and shipment rate. Spatial analyses also indicate geographically heterogeneous post-registration changes among other dried-persimmon-producing prefectures. The findings suggest that GI registration may affect rural production systems not only through brand protection but also through changes in commercialisation and institutional governance. More broadly, the study highlights the importance of evaluating layered intellectual property protection as an institutional component of rural development policy whose implications may differ across production and market participation.

items.title: Winter injury of red raspberry ( Rubus idaeus L.) buds under commercial field conditions: Relationships with temperature, spur blight and biochemical traits
items.authors: Maire Tõrra, H. Kaldmäe, P. Põldma, I. Reile, Kärolin Kork, A. Kikas
items.abstract: Winter injury limits raspberry ( Rubus idaeus L.) production in northern climates. This study evaluated the associations between winter injury, temperature, spur blight severity, and bud proline and soluble sugars contents in ‘Glen Ample’ raspberry grown in eight commercial plantations in Estonia over three winters: 2021/22, 2022/23, and 2023/24. Bud injury ranged from 18 to 98% among plantations and years, while neither minimum temperature nor the maximum number of consecutive hours below −25 °C accounted for this variation. A significant positive correlation was found between spur blight ( Xenodidymella applanata ) severity and winter injury ( r = 0.833). Proline and soluble carbohydrate levels in March were not consistent indicators of bud winter survival. These findings demonstrate that winter injury of raspberry buds is determined by interacting abiotic and biotic stress factors rather than by minimum temperature alone and growers should consider cane health alongside winter temperature in winter-injury risk assessments.

items.title: Dissecting the genetic basis of DUS characters in Pakistani wheat varieties
items.authors: Haq IU, Qureshi IA, Hussain MA, Javaid RA, Sheikh F, Abbas Z, Azam M.
items.abstract: Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability (DUS) testing is fundamental to varietal characterization and the protection of Plant Breeders’ Rights (PBRs), but conventional DUS assessment relies predominantly on morphological characteristics whose expression may be influenced by environmental conditions, developmental stage and observer-related variation. Integrating character-specific molecular markers with conventional DUS assessment may therefore improve the reproducibility and genetic resolution of varietal identification. This study investigated the genetic architecture of DUS characteristics in a panel of 102 historical and modern Pakistani wheat varieties using genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Phenotypic variation was evaluated using distribution, correlation and hierarchical clustering analyses, while the germplasm was genotyped using a wheat genotyping-by-targeted sequencing platform. After quality filtering, 21,670 high-quality single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were retained for analyses of genetic diversity, population structure, linkage disequilibrium (LD) and marker-trait associations. Population structure analysis indicated extensive admixture, with cross-entropy supporting K = 9 ancestral components, whereas hierarchical genetic clustering separated the germplasm into five broad groups. The first three principal components explained 8.09%, 7.20% and 5.39% of the total genetic variation, respectively. GWAS using BLINK and FarmCPU identified significant associations for several diagnostically important DUS characteristics. Growth habit was strongly associated with SNP 1B_129176704, with an additional signal on chromosome 5B. Shattering showed its strongest association at 1D_445256324, accompanied by several closely linked SNPs in the same region and a…

items.title: Formation of a chestnut-like aroma by blending fresh-scented and bean-scented green teas.
items.authors: Wang Y, Yu YY, Sun H, Cao QQ, Wang F, Zhang J, Wei Y, Xu YQ.
items.abstract: Chestnut-like aroma is a favorable quality attribute of green tea. This study developed chestnut-like tea by blending fresh-scented Anji white tea (AJWT) with bean-scented Longjing green tea (LJGT). Sensory evaluation showed that increasing LJGT shifted the dominant aroma from fresh to chestnut-like and then bean-like, with 40% LJGT producing the most pronounced chestnut-like character. GC-O-MS combined with variable importance in projection (VIP) and relative odor activity value analyses (rOAVs) identified 13 key differential aroma-active compounds (VIP > 1; rOAV >1) among 137 volatiles, representing fresh, floral, and roasty notes. Aroma reconstitution associated the chestnut-like character with an rOAV-based distribution of approximately 75% fresh, 19% floral, and 6% roasty compounds. Addition experiments further suggested that cis-3-hexenyl hexanoate, β-myrcene, ethyl hexanoate, β-ionone, 2-pentylfuran, and 3-methylbutanal were associated with the aroma transition from fresh to chestnut-like. These findings support targeted regulation and blending of chestnut-like green tea aroma.

items.title: Traditional Plant Knowledge across Rural and Peri-Urban Istanbul: Documented Plants and Uses
items.authors: Emine Akalın, Rabia Ebrar Akıncı, Aybüke Kızılırmaklı Demir, O. Demir, E. Cabi
items.abstract: Purpose: This study examines traditional plant knowledge in rural and peri-urban Istanbul, where environmental access, household production and metropolitan connections coexist.Method: Fieldwork within Türkiye’s national programme for documenting traditional knowledge associated with bio-logical diversity covered 30 neighbourhoods in ten districts in 2021–2022. Purposive selection and local referrals iden-tified 112 informants contributing 667 plant-use reports. Original descriptions were retained alongside standardized taxonomic and use fields. Analyses examined repertoire composition, citation frequency, multifunctionality and district overlap. Retrospective taxon-level classifications distinguished predominantly wild-gathered from cultivated, managed, planted or otherwise obtained taxa, and identified a conservative subset confirmed in Istanbul flora sources. District overlap was assessed using an informant-block permutation model; sampling-adequacy estimates were exploratory.Findings: The repertoire comprises 174 taxa in 129 genera and 52 families, spanning 52 use categories, 25 plant-part groups and 12 preparation groups. Food accounted for 55.2% of reports, human health for 22.3% and household and material uses for 11.8%. Fruit and aerial parts predominated; cooking and raw use were the leading preparations. Tilia tomentosa led food citations, Olea europaea health and Castanea sativa household and material uses. The null model largely reproduced the raw increase in district overlap from taxa to preparations. Lower-than-expected preparation over-lap did not survive multiple-testing correction. Reports involving predominantly wild-gathered taxa accounted for 52.9%; their share was higher in food than health, but taxon-level permutation did not support a systematic d…

items.title: Agro-morphological Characterisation of Rice (Oryza sativa L.) Germplasm Accessions Using DUS Descriptors
items.journal: Plant cell biotechnology and molecular biology
items.authors: Priya Gupta, D. Gauraha, Jyoti Sahu
items.abstract: The present investigation was undertaken to characterise 200 rice germplasm accessions, along with seven checks, for visually assessed DUS (Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability) traits. The 207 entries were evaluated during Kharif 2020 in an augmented design with four blocks at the Research cum Instructional Farm, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur (Chhattisgarh), at a spacing of 20 cm × 15 cm with the recommended package of practices under normal irrigated conditions (no drought stress was imposed). Observations were recorded on twenty-four DUS descriptors. Of these, one descriptor (shape of ligule) was monomorphic, nine were dimorphic and fourteen were polymorphic. Based on the Shannon–Weaver diversity index, hull colour, flag leaf attitude, panicle exsertion, grain breadth and basal leaf sheath colour were the most variable descriptors. Unique accessions such as IC390636 (aromatic) and IC516693 (red lemma) were identified, which may be useful as donors and in candidate variety development. The study provides a morphological baseline for future drought-stress evaluation; drought tolerance itself was not assessed

items.title: Seasonal hypoxia and nitrate depletion in water chestnut (Trapa natans) beds: Implications for nitrogen cycling.
items.authors: Simmons W, Blossey B, Walter MT.
items.abstract: Dense beds of floating macrophytes can alter water quality by modifying dissolved oxygen (DO) and nitrogen (N) dynamics. Water chestnut (Trapa natans L.), a non-native annual macrophyte, forms extensive seasonal beds in freshwater systems in North America. The species is intensively managed to reduce negative impacts on native species, yet its effects on DO and nitrate (NO 3 - ) remain poorly studied. We quantified DO and NO 3 - -N concentrations inside and outside of three riverine T. natans beds in New York over three growing seasons. In addition, we assessed denitrification using field-collected water and sediment in laboratory microcosm incubations. During summer months, DO of water from within T. natans beds was 76% lower on average (1.28 mg L - 1 ) compared to outside beds (5.43 mg L - 1 ). For NO 3 - -N, concentrations averaged 0.45 (2017) and 0.11 (2018) mg L - 1 outside beds, but were depleted to 0.10 (2017) and 0.01 (2018) mg L - 1 within beds, 77%-88% lower than outside beds. In 2018, 60% of samples, mostly from within beds of T. natans, were below the analytical detection limit of NO 3 - -N (0.02 mg L - 1 ). Laboratory microcosm incubations did not detect consistent N 2 production, despite experimental nitrate enrichment. Together, these results show that T. natans beds create seasonally hypoxic, nitrate-depleted conditions. However, weak and inconsistent N 2 production in our incubation experiments indicates that additional studies are needed to further assess the fate of nitrogen within T. natans beds and whether management may involve potential tradeoffs between habitat quality and nutrient cycling.

items.title: A Validated LNA ‐Modified Probe‐Based qPCR Assay for the Fast and Accurate Detection of the Root Rot Pathogen Phytophthora × cambivora on Mycelial DNA and Artificially Inoculated Chestnut Tissue
items.authors: Viola Papini, Alessandra Benigno, M. Moriconi, D. Rizzo, Salvatore Moricca, Francesco Bigazzi
items.abstract: Phytophthora × cambivora is a destructive, hybrid pathogen that has plagued European forests and agroforestry systems for at least two centuries. This polyphagous oomycete, known as the causal agent of ink disease, is responsible for the decline of chestnut forests and orchards, as well as beech and oak stands. Its widespread occurrence in nurseries, traded propagation material, soil, irrigation basins, puddles along forest tracks, and watercourses increases the risk of local and long‐distance spread. Traditional identification methods based on symptom assessment, baiting and isolation on selective media no longer meet modern diagnostic requirements because they are time‐consuming, require specialised mycological expertise and often lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity. Currently, there are few methods available that use real‐time PCR to detect and quantify the pathogen. A new quantitative real‐time PCR (qPCR) assay that uses a locked nucleic acid (LNA) probe has been developed and validated on artificially infected chestnut tissue to address this issue. Our assay targeted a mitochondrial intergenic region between the NAD7 and COX3 genes. The primers and probe were designed using the OligoArchitect software. Specificity assays tested the target against a wide range of oomycetes, with validation carried out according to EPPO standard PM7/98. This method detects low levels of P. × cambivora DNA in infected chestnut tissue with a detection limit of 600 fg/μL, close to that of purified DNA. This qPCR‐LNA assay offers a fast, specific and robust tool for pathogen detection in a variety of applications, including routine diagnostics in nurseries and other vulnerable settings.

items.title: The Effect of Tannin Powder Supplementation in the Ration on Hematological Profiles and Blood Urea Nitrogen of Priangan Sheep
items.authors: Najwa Hegyra Gumilar, I. Hernaman, D. Latipudin, Ghistavera Izvantika
items.abstract: The use of dietary tannins as natural feed additives to regulate rumen protein degradation and improve nitrogen metabolism has been increasingly explored. Nevertheless, the evidence concerning the combined use of chestnut (Castanea sativa) and quebracho (Schinopsis lorentzii) tannin extracts in Priangan sheep is still limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of a commercial tannin powder containing these two plant extracts on Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) concentration and hematological profiles in Priangan sheep. Eighteen healthy male Priangan sheep with an initial average body weight of 19.64±2.51 kg were randomly allocated into three dietary treatments in a Completely Randomized Design with six animals assigned to each treatment. The experimental diets consisted of a control ration (P0), control ration plus 1% tannin powder (P1) and control ration plus 2% tannin powder (P2). Blood samples were taken for biochemical and hematological evaluation after 70 days of feeding. 2% tannin powder supplementation significantly increased BUN concentration compared to control and 1% supplementation groups (P 0.05). In general, supplementation with chestnut and quebracho tannin powder at the 2% inclusion level induced alterations in nitrogen metabolism without any measurable changes in the hematological status. The results of this study suggest that the tannin preparation tested can be included in the diet of Priangan sheep at up to 2% of dietary dry matter without causing adverse physiological effects.

items.title: Lipid and Secondary Metabolite Profile Changes During Cold Storage of Dongzao (Ziziphus jujuba Mill. cv. Dongzao): Responses to Postharvest Treatments and Implications for Marketability
items.authors: S. Yao, F. O. Holguin
items.abstract: Dongzao (Ziziphus jujuba Mill. cv. Dongzao) is a popular fresh-eating cultivar with a short shelf life at room temperature. As Dongzao acreage increases in the United States, extending the fresh-fruit supply window is important for commercial production. A preliminary study showed that Dongzao fruit began developing mold after approximately 5 weeks of cold storage. Therefore, a subsequent study evaluated the effects of an ethylene absorbent and two fungicides, Scholar and Mentor, on fruit quality, decay, and metabolomic changes during extended cold storage at 0 ± 0.5 °C. Compared with untreated fruit, the ethylene absorbent did not extend storage life or reduce decay, with more than 30% stem-end rot observed by week 6, suggesting that ethylene removal had limited effects on Dongzao storage deterioration. Both fungicides substantially reduced decay, but Scholar was more effective, with no stem-end rot detected after 9 weeks of storage. Heatmap and principal component analyses further showed that Scholar-treated fruit after 9 weeks clustered with fruit stored for 6 weeks, suggesting that Scholar treatment was associated with delayed metabolic changes accompanying advanced storage deterioration. Cold storage induced extensive lipid remodeling, with substantial increases in lipid metabolites, particularly lysophosphatidylcholines, lysophosphatidylethanolamines, and free fatty acids, indicating pronounced changes in membrane lipid metabolism under prolonged low-temperature storage. Cold storage also broadly altered secondary metabolism, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, alkaloids, and terpenoids. Although cold storage was the primary driver of metabolomic changes, Scholar treatment was associated with distinct alterations in flavonoid and terpenoid profiles after 9 weeks…

items.title: Free Amino Acid Composition in Various Organs, Fruit Maturity Stages, and Varieties of Jujube
items.authors: Chen Yang, Bi-Cong Li, Jin Yu, Xiao-Hua Yu, Ai-Ling Zhao, Xiao-Fang Xue
items.abstract: Jujubes ( Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) are rich in a variety of nutrients, among which free amino acids are important indicators, reflecting their nutritional quality and functional value. We investigated the dynamic changes in free amino acid contents during jujube fruit ripening, analyzed the differences among different organs and varieties, and provide a scientific basis for the quality evaluation and comprehensive utilization of amino acids in jujubes. Free amino acid contents in different jujube organs (fruit, flower, leaf), at five different developmental stages, and in the fruit of eight jujube varieties were determined using an automatic amino acid analyzer. Twelve free amino acids were detected in all tested samples, with total contents ranging from 50.35 to 76.26 mg/100 g fresh weight (FW). In terms of dynamic changes, in general the total free amino acid contents in fruit of the four varieties showed a decreasing trend and then an increase during ripening. Specifically, the total content was highest at the young fruit stage and second highest at the full-red stage in ‘Beijingsuanzao’. It was highest at the full-red stage and second greatest at the half-red stage in ‘Huanghuadongzao’, ‘Xinzhenghuizao’, and ‘Tailihong’. The total content was lowest at the expansion stage in ‘Tailihong’, but lowest at the white-ripe stage in the other three varieties. In terms of organ differences, the total free amino acid content in different organs followed the order fruit > flower > leaf. For varietal differences, the total free amino acid content in eight jujube varieties at the crisp-ripe stage differed significantly, ranging from 154.89 to 544.46 mg/100 g FW. The order from high to low was ‘Huanghuadongzao’ > ‘Tailihong’ > ‘Beijingsuanzao’ > ‘Jinsixiaozao’ > ‘Xinzhenghuizao’ > …
