items.title: First Vesicular Self-Assembly of Betulinic Acid and Its Applications.
items.authors: Sukhendu Kar, Soumen Patra, C. Yelamaggad, B. G. Bag
items.abstract: Betulinic acid (BA), a pentacyclic triterpenoid isolated from Ziziphus jujube, is demonstrated to undergo spontaneous vesicular self-assembly in aqueous-organic binary mixtures. This represents the first report of BA-based vesicles, with critical vesicular concentrations (CVC) of 30, 60, and 70 μM, respectively, determined in DMSO-water mixtures (1:1, 2:1, and 4:1 v/v), respectively. The morphology of the nano- to micro-scale architectures was characterized using optical microscopy, AFM, SEM, HRTEM, FTIR, and XRD. These vesicles effectively encapsulate diverse fluorophores and the chemotherapeutic agent doxorubicin. Controlled release studies highlight their potential for targeted drug delivery and the sequestering of toxic pollutants from waste water. Compared to free curcumin and BA alone, the curcumin-loaded BA vesicular self-assemblies showed significantly greater antimicrobial performance against both Gram-positive (S. aureus) and Gram-negative (E. coli) strains during disk diffusion assays. These findings establish betulinic acid vesicles as versatile, biobased platforms for potential therapeutic and environmental applications.

items.title: A Comparison of Two Species-Discriminatory SNP Sets for Taxonomic Assignment in Hybridizing European White Oaks (Quercus sect. Quercus).
items.authors: Rellstab C, Guichoux E, Gugerli F, Kremer A, Reutimann O.
items.abstract: Species identification is essential for conservation, forest management, and understanding ecological and evolutionary dynamics, such as adaptive introgression and maintenance of species boundaries in hybridizing taxa. Species-discriminatory marker sets have been shown to be more accurate than morphological identification, especially in hybridizing species complexes, and provide a more affordable alternative to genome-wide analyses. However, to our knowledge, no species complex exists for which several marker sets are available, let alone have been compared to each other. Moreover, it remains unclear how well marker sets can be applied to additional, closely related species. Here, we compared two independently developed SNP sets, one derived from amplicon sequencing and one from whole-genome sequencing, for three morphologically similar and hybridizing European white oak species sensu lato (Quercus robur, Q. petraea, and Q. pubescens). We applied the SNP sets to 560 samples, including samples of known pure ancestry, controlled crosses, natural populations, and four additional white oak species. Congruency between SNP sets was very high, but species assignment was slightly more accurate for the reference samples used in the development of the respective SNP set. Ancestry coefficients for first-generation hybrids were more precise with the SNP set based on whole-genome data. In a natural population, there was limited congruency between SNP sets in quantifying admixture. Notably, the SNP sets were able to identify up to two additional white oak species. Our study highlights the great potential of species-discriminatory SNP sets in science and practice, while demonstrating that ascertainment bias should not be neglected, and accurate introgression assessments may require ge…

items.authors: Ulagamadhavan Muthuraj
items.abstract: Siddha system of medicine offers several drugs for managing skin disorders, including contact dermatitis. Hence, a maiden attempt was made to repurpose an internal medicine for external application in chronic irritant contact dermatitis. A 30-year-old tea vendor with an 8-year history was treated with the drug, containing chestnut as its chief ingredient and occupational avoidance for 14 days. Complete resolution of dermatitis and symptoms was observed, with no recurrence during 12 months of drugless follow-up. However, well-designed clinical trials are required to evaluate its efficacy.

items.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Expression Analysis of ZjCDPK Genes Related to Ripening of ‘Dongzao’ Jujube Fruit
items.authors: Bing-Xin Fan, H. Li, Shi-Xing Wang, Su-Na Zhao, Zhao-Kun Zhi, Shu-Lin Zhang
items.abstract: Calcium-dependent protein kinases (CDPKs) are plant-specific Ca2+ sensors that translate calcium signals into phosphorylation responses. CDPKs coordinate both plant responses to the environment and plant growth, including fruit development and ripening. However, the CDPK gene family and its potential roles in jujube fruit development remain poorly characterized. In this study, 19 ZjCDPK genes were identified in the genome of ‘winter jujube’ (Ziziphus jujuba Mill. cv. ‘Dongzao’) and mapped to 11 of the 12 chromosomes. Phylogenetic analysis classified the ZjCDPK proteins into four groups, with CDPKs from Arabidopsis and tomato. Two intraspecific collinear gene pairs and sixteen orthologous gene pairs between ‘Dongzao’ and Arabidopsis were identified. Most family members exhibited similar organization of exon–intron splicing and contained similar motifs, with all containing a conserved serine/threonine protein kinase catalytic domain and four C-terminal EF-hand motifs. Promoter analysis identified 681 cis-acting elements, with abundant elements associated with abiotic stress, light, and phytohormone responses, including those related to abscisic acid, ethylene, methyl jasmonate, salicylic acid, auxin, and gibberellin. Developmental expression profiling across seven fruit stages, together with qRT-PCR validation, showed that ZjCDPK02, 08, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 19 accumulated preferentially during the late stages of fruit development. Correlation analysis further showed that ZjCDPK14 was strongly co-expressed with ZjCDPK02 (r = 0.96) and positively correlated with both fruit firmness (r = 0.907) and total soluble solids content (r = 0.816). Significant associations with these quality traits were also detected for ZjCDPK02, 04, 08, 15, 16, and 19. These findings provide a compr…

items.title: Seasonal variation in Korean school lunch menus using big data from the National Education Information System: an exploratory study.
items.authors: Shin J, Park E.
items.abstract: Objectives School meal programs in South Korea are a major public nutrition service and an important part of student diets. Although previous National Education Information System- based studies have described frequently served menu items and annual trends, nationwide evidence on how school lunch menus differ seasonally remains limited. Thus, in this exploratory study, we aimed to analyze summer-winter differences in frequently served items in South Korean elementary, middle, and high schools. Methods Nationwide school lunch records from 2023 to 2025 were obtained from the National School Meal Information application programming interface. Lunch meal units served in elementary, middle, and high schools were analyzed. The final dataset comprised 1,200,000 meal units. Menu items were classified into six categories: rice/noodles, soups/stews, kimchi, main dishes, side dishes, and desserts. In each category, items frequently served in summer and winter were identified, and seasonal differences were quantified using a seasonal gap index and z-tests. Results Seasonal variation was highest in kimchi and desserts. Among the top items, 25/26 kimchi items and 27/30 dessert items showed significant seasonal differences. In desserts, watermelon, oriental melon, and ice cream were strongly summer-dominant, whereas apple, strawberry, and sweet persimmon were winter-dominant. In kimchi, young summer radish kimchi and cucumber kimchi were summer-dominant, whereas diced radish kimchi and napa cabbage kimchi were winter-dominant. Rice/noodles, soups/stews, and side dishes showed moderate seasonal variation. Main dishes showed the lowest degree of seasonal variation, with all-time popular items displaying minimal variation. Conclusion Seasonal variation in menu items was concentrated in s…

items.title: Bezoars-Induced Small Bowel Obstructions due to Dried Persimmons that Required Multiple Surgeries: A Case Report.
items.authors: Yonenaga Y, Ito R.
items.abstract: Introduction A bezoar is an indigestible conglomeration trapped in the gastrointestinal tract. Persimmon phytobezoars, known as diospyrobezoars, are formed after the frequent consumption of persimmons and are a distinct type of phytobezoar characterized by their hard consistency. Case presentation A 74-year-old female presented to our hospital with persistent abdominal pain and vomiting, and an intestinal strangulating obstruction was suspected. An emergency operation was performed, and a dietary small bowel obstruction was diagnosed. A small intestinal resection, including removal of a foreign body resembling a sponge-like mass, was performed. During detailed questioning, we asked her about any history of persimmon ingestion, but she denied it. The symptoms recurred on POD 8, and another dietary small bowel obstruction was suspected after a CT examination. Conservative treatment, including Coca-Cola dissolution therapy, was performed, but the symptoms were not alleviated, and she developed a fever on POD 24. On POD 30-the 22nd day after the 2nd onset-she suddenly remembered that she had eaten 16 dried persimmons between 24 and 19 days before the onset of symptoms. A 2nd operation was performed the following day. Because feces were found in the abdominal cavity and the perforated site could not be found laparoscopically, we converted to laparotomy. At the location of the obstruction in the ileum, a foreign body and a perforation were seen, and a partial ileectomy was performed. The foreign body also resembled a sponge-like mass, and a component analysis showed that it consisted of 98% tannin. A diospyrobezoar was finally diagnosed. Conclusions Because multiple diospyrobezoars could exist in the gastrointestinal tract, we should check for additional bezoars throughout th…

items.title: Blackberry Leaf Blotch Virus, a Novel Emaravirus Infecting Cultivated and Wild Blackberry Plants in Europe.
items.authors: Hellin P, Richet P, Demonty E, de Koning PPM, de Krom C, den Hartog WGSA, Westenberg M, Botermans M, Druciarek T, Winter S, Rimbaud L, Dubuis N, Blouin AG, Kovačec E, Grubar B, Toplak N, Steyer S, Mav
items.abstract: A novel emaravirus provisionally named blackberry leaf blotch virus (BLBV), was identified from cultivated and wild blackberry plants ( Rubus sp.) exhibiting leaf blotch and vein banding/feathering symptoms. BLBV has been detected in Belgium, France, the Netherlands and Slovenia. The virus is most closely related to raspberry leaf blotch virus (RLBV, Emaravirus idaeobati ) infecting raspberry ( Rubus idaeus ) in Europe, and is distant from blackberry leaf mottle-associated virus (BLMaV, Emaravirus rubi ), infecting blackberry in the USA. Up to eight RNA segments were identified in BLBV isolates, including the four core RNA segments present in all emaraviruses and up to four additional non-core RNA segments. Spherical virus-like particles (70-90 nm), morphologically similar to emaravirus virions, were observed in sap from symptomatic blackberry tissue by transmission electron microscopy. The proteins encoded by the core RNA segments were all more than 20% divergent from their closest known emaravirus homologues, supporting the classification of BLBV as a new species. Genetic diversity was found among isolates even at the country level, with some additional RNA segments only detected for some isolates. Eriophyoid mites, known vectors of emaraviruses, were found on several infected plants and molecular barcoding identified the them as Epitrimerus gibbosus , an eriophyoid species previously reported on Rubus spp. in Europe. Transmission bioassays performed with these mites in a greenhouse supported E. gibbosus as a putative vector of BLBV. This discovery raises questions about the impact of BLBV on blackberry crops and the need for virus surveillance in plant propagation material.

items.title: Combined effects of drought and insect herbivory on oak leaf endophytic communities and performance.
items.authors: Barlier T, Castagneyrol B, Carton J, Burlett R, Bonnard O, Schimann H.
items.abstract: Leaf-associated microbiota are considered sensitive indicators of how plants respond to their environment. Yet, plants can be exposed to a wide range of biotic and abiotic stresses whose independent and combined effects on plant microbiota remain poorly understood, as do their cumulative consequences for plant performance. We conducted an experiment to expose saplings of four oak species to drought and herbivory by a piercing-sucking insect. We assessed the effect of water deficit on herbivory, as well as the individual and combined effects of water deficit and herbivory on fungal endophytic communities. To evaluate the cumulative impacts of biotic and abiotic stresses on plant performance, and the potential of the fungal endophytic communities as an indicator of plant responses to stress, we measured photosynthetic capacity, growth, and the accumulation of non-structural carbohydrates in twigs at the end of the growing season. Water deficit had no effect on insect herbivory but induced a decrease in the diversity of the leaf-associated fungal community. In contrast, herbivory shifted the composition of fungal communities through species replacement or addition depending on oak species. Herbivory altered photosynthesis, whereas drought but not herbivory reduced oak growth. None of these stresses influenced the storage of non-structural carbohydrates. Leaf-associated fungi responded to both stresses. However, the underlying mechanisms appeared to differ and the association with oak performance was weak. Overall, our study suggests a certain degree of resilience in trees subjected to interacting stresses, while also highlighting vulnerabilities that may have implications for tree health over the long term.

items.title: Profiling of pollen in honey using multispectral imaging flow cytometry.
items.authors: Walther F, Hofmann M, Janke M, Erler S, Friedrich E, Treder M, Rakosy D, Harpole WS, Mäder P, Berdún A, Hornick T, Dunker S.
items.abstract: Pollen identification from honey (melissopalynology) is of great economic and consumer relevance. Traditional microscopy is time-consuming and dependent on expert knowledge, thus limiting high-throughput analyses. We tested whether pollen images generated with Multispectral Imaging Flow Cytometry (MIFC) classified by machine learning (ML) (convolution neural networks (CNNs) and random forest (RF)) can serve as a fast and reproducible method for identifying pollen in honey. We examined how the classification of honey pollen is affected by images from different matrices (anther and honey samples), how results compare with traditional microscopic analysis and used a set of human-interpretable image features to better explain ML results. The study focused on the six common target pollen in honey Brassica, Castanea, Centaurea, Helianthus, Phacelia and Tilia type. A classifier trained with a combination of anther and honey brightfield and fluorescence images provided the best predictions for 13 monofloral and 10 polyfloral honeys. Yielding pollen identification results comparable to microscopy, three times more pollen can be evaluated, and a measurement time of a maximum of 10 min, the method demonstrates its high potential as a powerful screening tool in melissopalynology.

items.title: Effects of individual and combined plant-extract treatments on the mechanical properties of sheepskin leather
items.authors: M. Mels, B. Bitlisli, L. Sarttarova, Bekzhan Abzalbekuly, Jakhongir Gafurov, A. Tortay
items.abstract: The object of the study was the technology of treating sheepskin leather intended for footwear manufacture with natural plant extracts, with particular attention to its mechanical performance. The problem was to select a binary treatment that would balance tensile strength, tear resistance, and elongation at break, because these properties do not necessarily respond in the same way to increasing extract concentration. The study examined chrome-tanned sheepskin leather treated with plant extracts for potential use as a footwear material. Individual oak bark, agrimony, horse chestnut, and chlorophyll treatments and binary combinations were first compared. Oak bark and horse chestnut extracts were then studied at concentrations of 1.5–2.5% each. Regression models and multi-response optimization were used to examine concentration-dependent changes and select a treatment condition within this range. Oak bark gave the highest tensile strength among the individual treatments, whereas the oak bark–horse chestnut combination gave the highest tear resistance among the screened treatments. In the concentration experiment, higher oak bark levels favored tensile strength, tear resistance showed a curved response to horse chestnut concentration, and elongation decreased towards higher extract concentrations. A treatment with 2.0% oak bark and 2.25% horse chestnut was selected as a compromise among the three responses (overall desirability 0.65697). At this condition, experimental tensile strength, tear resistance, and elongation were 8.605 ± 0.17 N/mm2, 40.707 ± 0.81 N/mm, and 48.725 ± 0.97%, respectively. Relative prediction errors were 1.55%, 1.94%, and 1.77% (mean 1.75%). These results provide a basis for selecting extract concentrations for the tested sheepskin under laboratory c…

items.title: Phenotypic Characterization and Transcriptomic Profiling of Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa Seedlings Under ATP Treatment and Identification of a Novel Lupeol Synthase
items.authors: Yan-Sheng Wu, Shen-Xiu Du, Hua-Liang Liu, Yi-Mian Ma, Wen-Jing Wang, Ye-Lin Tian
items.abstract: The tender leaves of Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa (sour jujube) are widely consumed in China as a health-promoting tea, with triterpenoids being identified as one of their core bioactive constituents. However, key genes in the triterpenoid biosynthesis pathway remain largely uncharacterized in this species. Here, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) treatment inhibited sour jujube seedling growth, induced leaf curling and marginal withering in partial seedlings, and elevated triterpenoid content in seedling aboveground tissues. Transcriptome analysis showed that most mevalonic acid (MVA) pathway enzyme genes were not significantly altered, while some were downregulated, and some enzyme isoforms were slightly upregulated. Combined genome and transcriptome analysis identified one slightly upregulated oxidosqualene cyclase (OSC) gene, ZsLUS, among 13 sour jujube OSC family genes. Heterologous expression in yeast confirmed that ZsLUS encodes a bona fide lupeol synthase with catalytic activity. These results indicate that ATP treatment enhances triterpenoid accumulation without uniformly upregulating MVA pathway genes, suggesting a sub-pathway-specific regulatory mode or post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism for triterpenoid biosynthesis in sour jujube seedlings. This work deepens our understanding of the mechanism of ATP action on sour jujube triterpenoid biosynthesis and provides new clues for deciphering triterpenoid biosynthesis and accumulation in sour jujube leaves.

items.title: Sirdaryo viloyati sharoitida chilonjiydaning istiqbolli navlari ko'chatlarini yetishtirish texnologiyasini takomillashtirish
items.authors: Jasur Eshquvvatov
items.abstract: This article analyzes the scientific basis for improving the technology of growing seedlings of promising jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) cultivars under the conditions of the Syrdarya region of Uzbekistan. The relevance of the study is associated with the adaptability of jujube to arid and continental climatic conditions, the nutritional and biological value of its fruits, and the increasing interest in expanding jujube cultivation in Uzbekistan. Scientific information on jujube cultivars introduced into Uzbekistan, seed and vegetative propagation methods, pre-sowing seed treatments, cutting rooting, and grafting techniques used for the production of planting material is reviewed. Previous research conducted under Uzbek conditions investigated nine jujube cultivars introduced from China, including Xiangzao, Zanhuangdazao, Tangzao, Mayabaizao, Junzao, Dabailing, Dongzao, Linyilizao, and Jixinzao, with several cultivars demonstrating promising adaptability. Recent research on seed propagation has also demonstrated the importance of pre-sowing treatment and sowing depth. Under the conditions of the Republic of Karakalpakstan, the highest seed germination was observed at a sowing depth of 2.5–3.0 cm, while scarification accelerated seed germination and improved germination performance. Studies of vegetative propagation have demonstrated that indole-3-butyric acid (IBA) can significantly improve the rooting of jujube cuttings and root development characteristics. The reviewed scientific evidence provides a basis for developing an adapted technology for producing high-quality jujube planting material under the soil and climatic conditions of the Syrdarya region.

items.title: Legal Challenges in the Registration of Farmers' Varieties under the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001
items.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
items.authors: V. M. Kandiyar
items.abstract: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001 (PPV&FR Act) is the intellectual property framework developed by India to protect plant varieties while taking into account the role of farmers in agricultural innovation and the conservation of biodiversity. However, many problems remain in the registration of farmers’ varieties. This paper examines whether the existing registration regime is able to protect traditional farmers’ varieties, given that the registration system is predominantly based on formal and standardized plant variety protection. The main emphasis is on the problems farmers face in fulfilling the criteria of distinctiveness, uniformity and stability (DUS) when traditional varieties contain genetic diversity and have developed over generations of farmers. The procedural, technical, evidential and financial problems of registration are also analyzed, along with the question whether small farmers can fulfill all the requirements. The paper further discusses the limited time period for the registration of farmers’ varieties. It also explores the role of traditional farmers in the plant variety protection regime, especially traditional farmers who have conserved, developed or improved such traditional varieties and may also be recognized as breeders. The recognition of such farmers as breeders raises issues about the kind of rights they hold as breeders and the possible conflict between their rights as traditional farmers and their rights under plant variety protection. The study asks whether the present regime properly balances the intellectual property rights of farmers as breeders, on the one hand, and their traditional practices of cultivating, using, exchanging and conserving plant varieties, on the other.

items.title: A new species of the genus Dysommina from the Lakshadweep Sea, India (Anguilliformes: Synaphobranchidae: Ilyophinae).
items.authors: Kodeeswaran P.
items.abstract: This study describes a new Dysommina species, based on two specimens collected at a depth of ca. 600 m in the Lakshadweep Sea off south-western India. The new species differs from its congeners in having fewer total vertebrae (120-127 vs. 134 in D. castanea, 133-134 in D. brevis, and 137-141 in D. orientalis), fewer predorsal vertebrae (14-15 vs. 16 in D. pygmaea), fewer preanal vertebrae (24-27 vs. 28-31 in D. rugosa), and in a combination of morphometric, meristic, dentition and colouration characters. DNA sequences were generated and analysed.

items.title: Somatic embryogenesis from leaf segments of Quercus castanea Mill.
items.authors: C. Castillo-Martínez, E. Velasco-Bautista, M. Vallejo-Reyna, M. T. González-Arnao, Lizbeth Fernández-Cruz
items.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the capacity of leaf segments obtained from young shoots collected from adult Quercus castanea Mill. trees to form embryogenic callus and somatic embryos under in vitro conditions. Design/methodology/approach: The study was conducted in two stages. In the first stage, two culture media were compared to induce embryogenic callus and somatic embryos from leaf segments. In the second stage, the medium that produced the best response was evaluated under two incubation conditions, light and darkness, to determine their effect on callus growth and somatic embryo development. Results: In the first stage, WPM medium supplemented with 0.5 mg L⁻¹ 2,4-D showed the best response, with 82% embryogenic callus formation and 32% somatic embryo formation. In the second stage, no statistically significant differences were detected between light and darkness, indicating that these conditions did not substantially did not significantly affect callus volume.. Somatic embryos maturation reached 95%after transfer to MS medium without growth regulators and supplemented with 100 mg L⁻¹ polyvinylpyrrolidone. Limitations/implications: The study was conducted under controlled in vitro culture conditions and focused on the response of leaf explants obtained from young shoots of adult trees; therefore, further studies are required to strengthen the protocol and evaluate its reproducibility under broader experimental conditions. Findings/conclusions: Leaf segments of Q. castanea constitute a viable source of explants for the induction of somatic embryogenesis. WPM medium supplemented with 2,4-D promoted embryogenic callus induction and somatic embryo formation, whereas incubation under light or darkness did not significantly modify the response.

items.title: The Relationship of Cultivars, Structures and In Vitro Digestibility of Chinese Chestnut (Castanea henryi) Starches Treated with Low-Voltage Electrostatic Field Technology
items.authors: Feng Chen, Xian-Tong Wu, Wen-Can Luo, Jing Wang, Wei-Jing Zhuang, Wen-Sheng Chen
items.abstract: Low-voltage electrostatic field (LVEF) treatment is an emerging food preservation technology that exploits the physical effects of electrostatic fields; however, its mechanisms of action in nut crops remain poorly understood. This study investigated changes in starch structure, processing properties, and in vitro digestibility in five chestnut cultivars (Castanea henryi) from different regions of China (Chushuhong, Changmangzi, Youzhen, Hongzhenzi, and Huangzhen) following refrigeration treatment (RT) and LVEF treatment. LVEF increased the crystallinity and molecular order of chestnut starch. It also generally reduced free water content, peak viscosity (PV), breakdown viscosity (BV), and setback viscosity (SV), while increasing water-holding capacity. In addition, LVEF enhanced the resistance to shear and retrogradation, thereby improving starch processing performance. The TPA results showed that LVEF improved the textural properties of chestnut starch gels, supporting their suitability for gel-based foods. The responses varied among the cultivars. Compared with RT, LVEF reduced the particle size and free water content of Chushuhong starch by 19.56% and 18.41%, respectively. Chushuhong also exhibited the largest increase in crystallinity (31.34%), while the bound water content of its starch gel increased by 13.70%, indicating stronger responsiveness to LVEF. Overall, LVEF improved the processing performance of chestnut starch, although varietal differences in the responses were observed. LVEF-treated Chushuhong and Changmangzi starches exhibited favorable processing properties, indicating their suitability for developing processed chestnut products. items.title: Organic Acids and Bacterial Communities of Backslopped Sourdough Prepared with Japanese Pear (Pyrus pyrifolia Nakai) Infusion
items.authors: Riho Endo, Tsukasa Shiraishi, Mihoko Moto
items.abstract: Addition of fruit during sourdough preparation can lead to the development of distinctive bacterial communities and fermentation characteristics. However, sourdough preparation with Japanese pear infusion remains understudied. We prepared sourdough with Japanese pear infusion and evaluated its organic acid composition and bacterial community. Sourdough was passaged for up to 56 generations. pH decreased rapidly during the initial generations of backslopping and subsequently stabilized at 3.5 and 3.7. High-performance liquid chromatography analysis revealed that lactic and acetic acid were the major organic acids. The fermentation quotient in the 55th and 56th generations ranged from 0.64 to 0.70, indicating an acetic acid-dominant profile. Bacterial community analysis targeting the V3–V4 region of the 16S rDNA gene revealed Furfurilactobacillus rossiae and Acetobacter pasteurianus as the dominant taxa. Average nucleotide identity analysis identified the representative isolates as Furfurilactobacillus milii and Acetobacter pasteurianus subsp. pasteurianus, respectively. This descriptive study is limited by a small sample size, lack of a control group, initial bacterial community data, and limited statistical analysis. Nevertheless, under the experimental conditions of this study, relatively high acetic acid levels were observed in the analyzed sourdoughs, together with a bacterial community dominated by the genera Furfurilactobacillus and Acetobacter were observed as predominant genera.

items.title: Comparative genomic analysis for selected members of the Ophiostomatales: insights into biosynthetic gene clusters and CAZymes.
items.authors: Abed S, Kumar A, Hausner G.
items.abstract: The Order Ophiostomatales includes ecologically diverse fungi, and many are associates of bark and/or ambrosia beetles. This order includes species that cause tree diseases, and many members are sapwood staining fungi. Despite their ecological and economic importance, the genomic basis of their adaptations remains poorly understood. Here, we present annotated genome assemblies for six species (seven strains) spanning three genera within the Ophiostomatales. Genomes ranged from 21 to 32 Mb with high completeness scores. CAZyme analyses revealed broadly conserved repertoires dominated by glycoside hydrolases and glycosyltransferases, with substantial representation of lignin-and cellulose-associated enzymes and marked quantitative variation among taxa, including expanded oxidative auxiliary activity families in Ophiostoma quercus and Leptographium truncatum and a reduced profile in Ceratocystiopsis minima. antiSMASH predicted 12-19 biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) among the seven genomes. Rather than only broad metabolite classes, comparative analysis revealed conservation of specific secondary metabolite families, including a putative 1,8-dihydroxynaphthalene (DHN) melanin cluster present in all genomes, a conserved fujikurin-like type I polyketide synthase (T1PKS) cluster present in all genomes except L. truncatum, and an Ophiostoma-specific NRPSbased metallophore/siderophore-like cluster potentially involved in iron acquisition. The genomic data provide new insights into the metabolic capacity and potential ecological differentiation of the Ophiostomatales.

items.title: Comparative Analyses of the Organellar Genomes of Quercus Reveal Contrasting Evolutionary Dynamics
items.authors: Si-Nuo Feng, Yu Li, Yi-Gang Song
items.abstract: Background: Mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes in plants have experienced distinct evolutionary trajectories due to differences in genomic organization, functional constraints, and genome maintenance mechanisms. However, comparative studies of their evolutionary dynamics in oaks remain limited. Methods: The complete mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes of Quercus arbutifolia were assembled and annotated using PacBio HiFi reads. Genome structure, repetitive sequences, codon usage, and mitochondrial plastid DNA transfers (MTPTs) were characterized. Evolutionary genomic and phylogenetic analyses were conducted across selected Quercus species to assess structural variation, sequence divergence, and phylogenetic relationships. Results: The mitochondrial genome of Q. arbutifolia was assembled as a 493,735 bp linear molecule, whereas the chloroplast genome was assembled as a 160,682 bp circular molecule. The mitochondrial genome exhibited lower coding density and a higher abundance of repetitive sequences than the chloroplast genome. Both organellar genomes preferentially used A/U-ending codons, with codon usage variation associated with mutation bias and selective constraints. Thirty-two MTPT regions were identified, predominantly representing plastid-to-mitochondrial transfers. Chloroplast genomes showed conserved inverted repeat boundaries among Quercus species, whereas mitochondrial genomes displayed extensive structural rearrangements, indicating contrasting evolutionary dynamics between the two organellar genomes. Nucleotide diversity analyses further revealed different sequence variation between organellar genomes, with chloroplast protein-coding genes (PCGs) generally exhibiting higher sequence divergence than mitochondrial PCGs. items.title: Testing the Potential of <i>Pseudomonas</i> Bacteria for the Biocontrol of Ink Disease of Chestnut.
items.authors: Dennert F, Troxler V, Bossert OX, Schneider S, Maurhofer M, Prospero S.
items.abstract: Ink disease, caused by the two oomycetes Phytophthora cinnamomi and Phytophthora × cambivora , is one of the most devastating diseases of sweet chestnut ( Castanea sativa ) in Europe. Its control is particularly difficult, with few fungicides showing a satisfactory effect, and those being progressively banned in forest ecosystems or in forest-like plantations because of ecological concerns. Therefore, alternative, nature-friendly control methods are urgently needed. The bacterial genus Pseudomonas includes many species with antifungal and antimicrobial properties. In this study, we isolated Pseudomonas bacteria from the rhizosphere of healthy and diseased chestnut trees in southern Switzerland. Out of 166 isolated Pseudomonas strains, 5 showed significant growth inhibition of P . cinnamomi and/or P . × cambivora in vitro. Three strains that significantly inhibited the growth of both pathogens were tested against a collection of 20 isolates of each species, showing that the in vitro inhibition is independent of the pathogen isolate. The mechanisms underlying this inhibition remain unclear because none of the three strains harbored biosynthesis genes coding for well-known antimicrobial secondary metabolites. Phylogenetic analysis of whole genome sequences showed that two of the strains belong to the P . fluorescens subgroup, whereas one strain probably belongs to a previously unrecognized species closely related to the P . putida subgroup. The results of this study indicate that Pseudomonas have the potential to be used as biocontrol agents against ink disease. Further experiments are needed to confirm their inhibitory effect against P . cinnamomi and P . × cambivora in vivo.

items.title: Identification and Expression Profiling of Olfactory-Related Genes in Exolontha castanea (Coleoptera: Melolonthinae) Using Tissue-Specific Transcriptomics
items.authors: Wen-Jing He, Yu-Xin Yang, Cheng-Hua Huang, Xue-Hong Pan, Gen Xia, Zi-Xuan Wu
items.abstract: Exolontha castanea is an important subterranean pest of sugarcane in China, currently controlled mainly by chemical insecticides. However, prolonged and improperly timed insecticide application has exacerbated infestations, necessitating the development of eco-friendly management strategies. Given the pivotal role of olfactory-related genes in host-seeking, mating, and oviposition, deciphering the olfactory mechanisms of E. castanea may support environmentally sound pest management. In this study, we sequenced transcriptomes from different tissues of male and female E. castanea and annotated olfactory-related genes. We identified 35 odorant binding proteins (OBPs), 12 chemosensory proteins (CSPs), 51 odorant receptors (ORs), 21 ionotropic receptors (IRs), and 4 sensory neuron membrane proteins (SNMPs). Expression profiling indicated that 13 OBPs, 6 CSPs, 16 ORs, 5 IRs, and 2 SNMPs were moderately or highly expressed in the antennae, and among these, 4 OBPs, 4 CSPs, 1 IR and 1 SNMP were also moderately or highly expressed in non-olfactory tissues. In addition, 8 OBPs, 1 CSP, 5 IRs and 1 SNMP displayed moderate or high expression levels only in non-olfactory tissues, including the head, leg, thorax, and abdomen. Based on these findings, the potential functions of these olfactory-related genes are discussed. This study represents the first comprehensive catalog of olfactory-related genes in E. castanea, laying a solid foundation for future functional characterization and novel sustainable pest management strategy development.

This study evaluated the physicochemical profiles and antimicrobial efficacy of five monofloral Pakistani honeys, namely Helianthus annuus L. Proline content (≥180 mg/kg), diastase numbers (DN) (10.0 ± 0.46 to 39.32 ± 0.58 DN), and invertase activity IN (63.00 ± 8.70 to 75.33 ± 5.70 IN) confirmed the freshness and purity of the honeys. items.title: Research on Image Enhancement of Crisp-Ripe Stage Red Jujube Based on Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
items.authors: Qi-Hang Yuan, Long Wang, Lu Shi, Qiao-Nan Yang, Yong-De Zhang
items.abstract: Machine vision technology plays a crucial role in non-destructive detection and online monitoring of deep processing for red dates during the crisp-ripe stage. However, due to factors such as uneven illumination in the collection environment and illumination attenuation on the curved surface of quasi-spherical objects, the collected images of red dates during the crisp-ripe stage often suffer from issues such as low overall image quality, difficulty in recognizing epidermal fruit spots and fine textures, low contrast between fruit surface crack defects and normal fruit surfaces, and blurred fruit body edges, which increase the difficulty of accurately identifying fruit surface features. In response to the common problems of over-enhancement and loss of details in current image enhancement methods when processing images of red dates during the crisp-ripe stage, this paper combines the practical requirements of preserving details of the fruit body and crack edges, enhancing epidermal texture clarity, balancing contrast and noise, and constructs a multi-dimensional image enhancement fitness function. A method for enhancing images of red dates during the crisp-ripe stage based on the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is proposed. Through comparative experiments on image enhancement of red dates during the crisp-ripe stage, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed image enhancement method are verified from both subjective visual effects and objective evaluation indicators.

items.title: Agricultural Waste-derived bio-sorbents used for the analysis of UV filters in sea water samples: An in-depth comparison with commercial sorbents.
items.authors: Voutsas P, Perrucci M, Locatelli M, Tolkou AK, Samanidou V.
items.abstract: The development of sustainable sample preparation strategies is increasingly important for reducing the environmental footprint of analytical methods. In this study, waste-derived biosorbents were investigated as low-cost and green alternatives to commercial materials for the extraction of organic UV filters from sea water samples. Banana (BAN), lime, orange, and pomegranate peels, alongside with activated carbon derived from waste chestnut shells (ACCHE), were evaluated for the extraction efficiency of oxybenzone, enzacamene, avobenzone, octocrylene, and ethylhexyl salicylate. BAN and ACCHE exhibited the highest adsorption performance, with BAN selected for further optimization. A dispersive solid-phase extraction (d-SPE) procedure using BAN as sorbent, coupled with HPLC- DAD was developed and validated. The method demonstrated good linearity (R² > 0.99), relative recoveries of 84.4-106.8% in intra-day study and 88.8-103.6% in inter-day study, and satisfactory precision (RSD: 0.7-12.6%). Natural sorbents BAN and ACCHE were also compared with commercial SPE sorbents, Oasis HLB, LiChrolut RP-18, and Discovery C18 and showed comparable extraction performance. The optimised method was applied to seawater samples to confirm its suitability, with avobenzone and octocrylene detected at sub-ng/mL concentrations in samples collected during the summer season. Green analytical metrics (RAPI, ComplexMoGAPI, BAGI and VIGI) were utilised to further support the sustainability, practicality, robustness and innovation of the proposed method. items.title: Constructing restructured jujube using blackened jujube pulp and carrageenan to resolve Peel-induced rough mouthfeel.
items.authors: Zhang H, Wang Y, Sun X, Gao L, Zhang D, Zhang R.
items.abstract: Blackened jujube offers improved nutritional value, while its peel-induced coarse mouthfeel limits its broader use in snack-style products. To address this limitation, this study proposes restructuring blackened jujube pulp into self-supporting composite gels using κ-carrageenan (KC). While neither 0.5% KC nor the pulp alone formed a self-supporting gel, composite gels containing 0.5% KC were observed to be self-supporting, indicating that the pulp matrix facilitates gelation at a lower KC level. Increasing KC from 0.5% to 2.5% progressively strengthened the network, increasing hardness from ~2.5 N to 16.7 N, water-holding capacity from 53.45% to 77.01%, and freeze-thaw syneresis from 68.94% to 26.69%, alongside network densification and T₂₂ shortening (75.8 to 37.0 ms). Sensory evaluation also confirmed that restructuring markedly reduced grittiness and improved overall mouthfeel. Overall, this work offers a practical strategy for converting fruit pulps into self-supporting composite gels, thereby enabling blackened jujube products with tunable texture and improved mouthfeel. The authors contributed equally to this work.

items.abstract: Precise characterisation of genotypes helps identify distinct morphological traits, minimise varietal mixtures and select suitable genotypes for hybridisation. The present study was conducted at Dr. YS Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry, Nauni, Solan (H.P.), during 2022–2023, involving morphological characterisation of 14 gladiolus genotypes using 66 distinctness, uniformity and stability (DUS) descriptors standardised by the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority (PPV&FRA). The experiment was conducted in a randomised block design with three replications. A considerable amount of variability was detected for the studied vegetative, floral and corm traits with genotypes showing maximum variation for 21 traits comprising three continuous variables: plant height, corm weight before and after storage which subsequently contributed maximum to variability, that is, 4.24%, 4.23% and 4.35% respectively along dimension 1, and several categorical variables with anther: colour of stomium (6.09%) and outer bract: anthocyanin colouration (5.91%) as key contributors along dimension 2, as confirmed by factor analysis of mixed data (FAMD). The first five dimensions accounted for >60% of the total variation, with dimensions 1 and 2 explaining 17.4% and 13.9%, respectively. Hierarchical Clustering on Principal Components (HCPC) grouped the genotypes into seven clusters, whereas unweighted pair group method with arithmetic mean (UPGMA) generated three major clusters, with considerable similarity in grouping. items.title: Advancing DUS characterization of neem through systematic gap analysis and setting future research priorities
items.authors: Aman Mahajan, A. Rana, J. Jyoti, Yogendra Kumar, Rama Kant, Ashok Kumar
items.abstract: Azadirachta indica A. Juss. (neem) is a multipurpose tree species of agricultural, medicinal, pesticidal and industrial importance. Increasing demand for neem-derived products, particularly neem oil for neem-coated urea, has stimulated genetic improvement programme for development of superior planting material with enhanced production and biochemical traits. In this context, Forest Research Institute (FRI), Dehradun, in collaboration with the Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative Limited (IFFCO), released six elite neem varieties characterized by early flowering and fruiting, with oil content ranging from 35.44 to 43.51% and azadirachtin content from 6047 to 9760 ppm. The development and release of such improved varieties necessitate reliable and standardized distinctness, uniformity and stability (DUS) characterization for their identification, registration and legal protection. However, application of DUS testing in neem is challenging because of its perennial growth habit, extended juvenile phase, phenotypic plasticity and environmental influence on morphological traits. This systematic review synthesizes available information on DUS characterization in neem and critically examines morphological, quantitative, pseudo-qualitative and biochemical descriptors used for varietal identification. It identifies limitations in existing descriptor framework and highlights need for systematic validation across environments and developmental stages. Importantly, review contextualizes neem DUS characterization within recent advances in varietal development and considers its broader utility in breeding, germplasm characterization, conservation, and variety protection. items.title: Construction of China’s Legal Protection System for New Animal Varieties
items.authors: F. Chong
items.abstract: While new animal breeds have long been at the center of advancing both animal husbandry and the broader bioeconomy, there is considerable confusion regarding their legal protection in China. While the Patent Law specifically excludes the patenting of new animal varieties, the Animal Husbandry Law has historically focused upon administrative approvals of breeds rather than the establishment of proprietary rights. For this reason, it is not surprising that a gap exists in the law, since breeders of new animal varieties (novel, distinct, uniform, and stable) currently lack an exclusive civil right that may be established, sold, or enforced. This paper considers the experience of the EU under the Biotech Directive and the U.S. dual regulatory model in protecting biotechnological innovations involving non-human animals. Drawing upon an analysis of both systems, it proposes a multi-tiered protection system for new animal breeds in China. It is argued that China needs to break free from the current binary division between protected/unprotected animal varieties versus patentable/unpatentable inventions derived from animals. The proposed multi-tiered protection system for new animal breeds is based on the level of technological intervention involved, along with the level of ethical concerns raised by each type of new animal variety. Animals bred using genetic editing techniques that do not involve the introduction of foreign DNA – and therefore represent lower risk from an ethical standpoint – should be protected through a sui generis Animal Breeder’s Right modeled on the existing Plant Variety Protection system. items.title: Molecular and morphological characterization of nine new Gnomoniopsis species ( Diaporthales , Gnomoniaceae ): Genomic insights into evolution and phylogeny.
items.authors: Wang X, Jiang Y, Liu W, Yan X, Sheng J, Ai C, Liu X, Zhang X, Meng Z, Wang S.
items.abstract: Gnomoniopsis comprises parasitic, endophytic, and saprophytic fungi. Since its establishment, this genus has presented considerable taxonomic challenges owing to extensive morphological overlap among species, rendering traditional classification systems that rely predominantly on phenotypic characteristics no longer applicable. To resolve the current taxonomic confusion and clarify the species diversity, phylogenetic relationships, and genomic adaptive characteristics of Gnomoniopsis, the present study was carried out. In this study, the internal transcriptional spacer (ITS), translation extension factor 1-α (tef1), and partial beta-tubulin (tub2) were analyzed and combined to observe morphological characteristics of Gnomoniopsis. The isolates were identified from chestnut (Castanea), Embelia vestita, tea (Camellia sinensis), and other hosts in Sichuan Province, as well as from Quercus species and partial leaf rot from Fujian Province. Nine new species, namely G. xiaoheijiangensissp. nov., G. embeliaesp. nov., G. yunvfengensissp. nov., G. quercussp. nov., G. ledongensissp. nov., G. yonganensissp. nov., G. conghuaensissp. nov., G. loropetalisp. nov., and G. qixiensissp. nov., were obtained. Phylogenomic analysis based on 7,942 orthologous proteins' clusters revealed distinct species boundaries within Gnomoniopsis. Phylogenomics has thus effectively resolved the ambiguous phylogenetic relationships in this genus. This work identifies nine previously undescribed Gnomoniopsis species, clarifies the species diversity and conserved genomic characteristics within the genus, and lays a foundation for subsequent taxonomic analyses of Gnomoniopsis.

items.title: Antioxidants and Trace Elements in Honey: A Positive Balance for Honeybees and Beekeeping Production
items.authors: C. Naccari, V. Ferrantelli, G. Cammilleri, Roberto Bava, E. Palma, Mariateresa Cristani
items.abstract: Antioxidants play a crucial role in preventing and treating various diseases in both humans and animals, and the consumption of nutraceuticals represents a major source of these compounds. Among nutraceuticals, special attention is focused on honey, which is the most widely used apicultural product due to its complex composition and several beneficial effects on humans and pets. Furthermore, it is a valid bio-indicator of environmental pollution within apiary foraging areas for the possible presence of pollutants, such as heavy metals, absorbed by honeybees. Particularly, the antioxidant contents and mineral profiles of honey are directly correlated with the floral origin of the nectar and, at the same time, influenced by climatic conditions, geo-chemical features and environmental pollution. items.title: Integrating Species Distribution Modelling and Spring Low-Temperature Exposure to Assess Climatic Suitability for Actinidia arguta in Europe
items.authors: Athanasios K. Margaritidis, Ioannis Charalampopoulos
items.abstract: Actinidia arguta (kiwiberry) is a cold-hardy perennial fruit crop with increasing cultivation interest outside its native East Asian range. This study assessed its climatic suitability across Europe using an ensemble species distribution modeling (SDM) framework calibrated with occurrence records from East Asia. After occurrence filtering and spatial thinning, 1483 presence records were retained. Twenty-one candidate environmental predictors were screened for multicollinearity and four variables—temperature seasonality (BIO4), maximum temperature of the warmest month (BIO5), precipitation seasonality (BIO15) and precipitation of the warmest quarter (BIO18)—were retained in the final SDM. Five algorithms (GLM, RF, MAXNET, GAM, GBM) were evaluated using environmental cross-validation and models meeting a TSS ≥ 0.60 threshold were combined in a TSS-weighted ensemble. Temperature seasonality showed the highest permutation importance (0.491), followed by precipitation of the warmest quarter (0.316). The European projection identified comparatively high climatic suitability primarily in parts of Central and Southeastern Europe, with approximately 68,226 km2 exceeding a suitability value of 0.50 and 21,634 km2 exceeding 0.60. Environmental clamping affected 10.2% of the European projection domain but only 0.4% of the area with suitability ≥ 0.50 and none of the area with suitability ≥ 0.60. A complementary March-May analysis of climatological minimum temperature showed that spring low-temperature exposure was strongly seasonal. items.title: Young persimmon fruit extract as a multifunctional natural additive in ice cream: Effects on physical properties, antioxidant functionality, and sensory acceptability.
items.authors: Kobayashi M, Hara T, Sunahara A, Ishigaki M, Tsurunaga Y.
items.abstract: Young persimmon fruit extract (YPE), a tannin-rich fruit-thinning by-product, was added to ice cream at added soluble tannin content (STC) levels of 0.0-1.0%. YPE imparted a natural reddish-brown color and significantly enhanced antioxidant activity without substantially altering pH or Brix. Microstructural, particle size, viscosity, and overrun analyses indicated that tannin-milk protein interactions densified the matrix and reduced air incorporation, improving melting resistance: complete melting required 51-54 min at 0.1-0.5% (peaking at 0.3%) added STC and 75 min at 1.0% added STC, versus 42 min for the control. Hardness, adhesiveness, and gumminess increased with added STC. Overall acceptability was maintained up to 0.5% added STC but declined at 1.0%, indicating a practical range of 0.1-0.5%. Exploratory sandwich ELISA showed a modest, concentration-dependent reduction in detectable casein and β-lactoglobulin content (up to 26%). YPE is a promising clean-label, multifunctional additive for valorizing an agricultural by-product.

items.title: Comparative Study of Soil Respiration Characteristics and Influencing Factors of Four Land-Use Types in the Aksu Desert–Oasis Ecotone
items.authors: Jia-Fei Liang, Hai-Lian Liang, Ruo-Xi Li, Lu-Qing Zhou, Wen-Jie Zhou, Fei Chen
items.abstract: Aims: Land-use types and soil salinization in arid desert–oasis ecotones are associated with differences in soil CO2 efflux, yet the combined effects of multiple environmental factors remain poorly understood. This study aims to characterise the seasonal patterns, temperature sensitivity, and major correlates of soil respiration across four typical land-use types, thereby supporting regional carbon budget assessments. Methods: We conducted in situ soil respiration monitoring during the 2024 growing season (April–October) in four representative habitats (Populus euphratica forest, jujube orchard, grassland, and wetland) in the Aksu desert–oasis ecotone, Xinjiang. Concurrent measurements of topsoil (0–20 cm) physicochemical properties and extracellular enzyme activities were taken. Pearson correlation, variation partitioning, and the Van’t Hoff temperature-response model were employed. Results: Soil respiration exhibited a unimodal seasonal pattern peaking in July, with growing-season mean fluxes ranked as grassland > wetland > jujube orchard > Populus euphratica forest. Temperature sensitivity (Q10) followed wetland (3.23) > grassland (2.44) > orchard (2.08) > forest (1.57), a pattern consistent with differences in soil moisture and salinity among the sites.
